articles.title: Germline pharmacogenomics of platinum, radiotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitor toxicity in non-small cell lung cancer: a mechanism-based systematic review and appraisal against CPIC evidence standards.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Germline variants predicting treatment toxicity guide care for a few drug-gene pairs, yet most reported associations never reach the clinic. Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) isolates the problem: somatic genotyping is standard and toxicity limits dose intensity across chemotherapy, radiotherapy and immunotherapy, yet no germline marker guides therapy. METHODS: Per a registered protocol (PROSPERO CRD420261364865), we searched four databases for 2020-2026 publications, synthesizing 35 studies from 15 countries. Thirty-four variant-toxicity associations were grouped by mechanism (transport/metabolism, DNA repair, immune regulation, target pathway). The 11 priority loci (12 variants) were benchmarked against the Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium (CPIC) hierarchy. RESULTS: Twenty-nine of 34 associations were nominally significant. Of 10 studies correcting for multiplicity, seven had a finding that passed its own threshold (the lead association in five). Of 12 studies with validation analyses, three mounted an independent attempt (two with stated reservations), all nominally positive (single SNP, FDR-adjusted p=0.179; polygenic score; 27 patients); none replicated an association passing a multiplicity threshold. Across 23 significant lead associations, effect magnitude decreased with sample size (Spearman ρ=-0.48, 95% CI -0.81 to -0.07), consistent with selection-driven inflation. XRCC1 rs25487 effects differed by treatment and endpoint. No priority locus reached CPIC level A or B for its NSCLC drug pair. CONCLUSIONS: Many germline toxicity biomarkers are reported in NSCLC, but evidence remains exploratory: validation is uncommon, effect-size inflation is plausible, and within the review window no candidate met implementation standards. The bottleneck is evidence maturation, not discovery. We propose a four-phase framework toward genotype-guided care.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Natural Product Pharmacology: From Molecular Discovery to Precision Therapeutics.
articles.abstract: The use of natural products as a chemically diverse source of bioactive molecules for drug development has been well established; however, their multicomponent and multitarget nature, uncertain target causality, variable in vivo exposure, and heterogeneous responses to therapy make them challenging to characterize pharmacologically and translate into clinical practice. Systems pharmacology, together with artificial intelligence (AI), provides new approaches for molecular screening, target prioritization, integration of multidimensional data, and development of precision therapeutics. Osteoarthritis (OA), a heterogeneous whole-joint disease characterized by inflammation, oxidative stress, metabolic dysfunction, and tissue remodeling, serves as a representative model for evaluating such approaches. Network pharmacology can be used to organize relationships among natural product constituents, disease-related targets, and signaling pathways. AI can further assist with activity prediction, compound and target prioritization, multi-omics integration, and patient stratification. Studies combining network pharmacology, molecular docking, deep-learning-based affinity prediction, and experimental validation to narrow the list of potential candidate constituents and targets demonstrate the utility of computational methods in candidate prioritization. This article describes the transition of natural product pharmacology from empirical discovery and systems-based analysis to AI-enabled molecular discovery, mechanistic interpretation, pharmacokinetic assessment, and precision therapeutics. Although computational approaches may facilitate the identification and prioritization of biologically active constituents and targets, they remain limited by uncertainty regarding causality, inadequate in vivo exposure, model dependence, and insufficient clinical evidence. Future studies should focus on precise active-compound identification, direct target validation, systematic pharmacokinetic assessment, and high-quality clinical research to enhance the reliability and translational value of AI-enabled natural product pharmacology.

articles.title: Impact of intermittent hypoxia on drug-metabolizing enzymes and transporters and drug pharmacokinetics: an underestimated concern in obstructive sleep apnea patients?
articles.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSA) is a prevalent and life-threatening respiratory disease. Marked by intermittent hypoxia (IH) and chronic inflammation, OSA frequently co-occurs with comorbidities like hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia or depression, necessitating various medications. However, the response to some treatments is notably compromised in OSA patients, manifesting as reduced efficacy and/or increased incidence of adverse events. The mechanisms underlying this altered pharmacological response remain unelucidated. Although comorbidities may substantially contribute to these alterations, IH and inflammation, key features of OSA, are known to modify drug-metabolizing enzymes and transporters (DMETs). We therefore hypothesized that OSA/IH may affect DMETs, thereby altering drug pharmacokinetics and drug response. This narrative review synthesizes existing literature regarding the impact of OSA/IH on DMETs and pharmacokinetics both in experimental models and human, along with the underlying mechanisms exploring the roles of pro-inflammatory cytokines, transcription factors and epigenetics. Subsequently, we discuss the potential consequences of these IH-induced DMETs alterations on drug response in OSA patient population. In this purpose, we examine the hypothesis of pharmacokinetic modifications for each drug (or pharmacotherapeutic class) whose response appears altered in OSA patients. Additionally, we analyze the pharmacokinetic profile of the most commonly dispensed medications in OSA patients in order to identify additional drugs whose efficacy or safety might be compromised by IH-induced DMETs alterations. Finally, in the absence of conclusive clinical evidence, we propose priority research areas to better characterize the impact of OSA/IH on DMETs, pharmacokinetics, and drug response, and the underlying mechanisms.

articles.title: A new chylomicron-independent pathway is responsible for intestinal lymphatic transport of the S1PR1 immunomodulator SEW2871.
articles.abstract: It is well recognized that the intestinal lymphatic transport of lipophilic drugs is primarily associated with chylomicron (CM) formation and transportation, a process that can be promoted by co-administration of lipids. Here, we report that the sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 1 (S1PR1) modulator SEW2871, an immunosuppressant that sequesters lymphocytes within lymphoid tissues, exhibits substantial lymphatic transport even in the absence of lipids, suggesting a CM-independent pathway. In thoracic lymph duct-cannulated rats, we compared the lymphatic transport of SEW2871 with the classic CM-dependent drug halofantrine following proximal small intestine (intraduodenal) administration. As expected, and consistent to documentations for typical lipophilic drugs in the literature, halofantrine showed high lymphatic transport with lipids (28.7%) but markedly lower (5.6-fold) transport without lipids (5.1%). In striking contrast, SEW2871 achieved very high lymphatic recovery (38.8% of the dose) in the absence of lipids. To further validate the CM-independent mechanism, we assessed SEW2871 absorption from the distal small intestine and subcutaneous tissue-sites incapable of endogenous CM formation. In both cases, SEW2871 maintained significant lymphatic recoveries of approximately 16% of the dose, whereas halofantrine transport was negligible under these conditions. Functionally, the enhanced lymphatic exposure after intraduodenal administration produced a markedly stronger inhibition of lymphocyte egress compared to the pharmacodynamic effect following intravenous infusion at the same dose, thereby demonstrating the therapeutic advantage of directly targeting the lymphatic system. Molecular docking revealed high binding affinity of SEW2871 to multiple macromolecules highly enriched in lymph, including albumin and apolipoprotein B isoforms, suggesting that SEW2871 may exploit alternative lymph-directing carriers to facilitate its uptake. Collectively, this study provides evidence for a new, CM-independent intestinal lymphatic transport pathway observed for SEW2871. Future elucidation of the exact mechanism may provide insights for developing next-generation lymph-targeted therapies.

articles.title: Vascular-targeted mild photothermal modulation of the blood-brain barrier enables efficient delivery of Pt(IV) prodrug to glioblastoma.
articles.abstract: Effective platinum chemotherapy for glioblastoma is constrained by the blood-brain barrier and blood-brain tumor barrier (BBB/BBTB), which limit intracranial drug exposure. Here, we developed PS@RGD-Pt nanoparticles that integrate a NIR photothermal semiconducting polymer, a reduction-responsive Pt(IV)-backbone polymer, and cRGD-functionalized PEG-PLGA to couple vascular targeting, mild photothermal barrier modulation, and intracellular platinum activation. In orthotopic GL261 gliomas, cRGD promoted nanoparticle localization at tumor-associated vessels. Irradiation by an 808 nm laser at 0.5 W/cm2 for 3 min raised the tumor-site temperature to 46.3 °C and transiently reorganized Claudin-5 and ZO-1. Extending irradiation to 6 min raised the temperature to 63 °C and induced glial activation, delineating a thermal-dose window. BBB/BBTB permeability peaked at 1 h and approached baseline within 24 h, without detectable alterations in vascular density, cerebral perfusion, neuronal or glial markers, memory, or locomotion. Within this mild photothermal window, intratumoral platinum accumulation increased by approximately 4.6-fold with low accumulation in the contralateral normal brain. Reduction-responsive activation of Pt(IV) enhanced tumor DNA damage and apoptosis. PS@RGD-Pt with irradiation prolonged median survival to 36 days, compared with 16 days for PBS, 20 days for nonirradiated PS@RGD-Pt, and 22 days for RGD-Pt with irradiation, while reducing systemic toxicity relative to cisplatin. These findings establish vascular-targeted, mild photothermal BBB modulation as a controllable strategy that couples reversible barrier opening with tumor-responsive platinum activation for glioblastoma treatment.

articles.title: Multi-omics and single-cell profiling characterize the protective effects of indole-3-acetic acid in hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is a major cause of liver dysfunction after hepatic surgery and transplantation. Sterile inflammation, myeloid-cell recruitment, and metabolic disturbance contribute to hepatic IRI, but effective immunometabolic interventions remain limited. Indole-3-acetic acid (3-IAA) is a natural plant auxin found in Arabidopsis thaliana shoot apices and young leaves and is also produced by microorganisms. Whether 3-IAA affects hepatic IRI is unknown. METHODS: We integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling to identify changes associated with hepatic IRI. We then evaluated 3-IAA pretreatment in a murine hepatic IRI model. Serum transaminases and histopathology were used to assess liver injury. CyTOF and single-cell RNA sequencing characterized immune-cell composition, functional signatures, and inferred intercellular communication. RESULTS: Untargeted metabolomic profiling identified 3-IAA among the metabolites showing lower hepatic abundance after IRI. 3-IAA pretreatment lowered alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase levels and reduced histological injury. CyTOF showed lower relative abundances of macrophages and neutrophils after 3-IAA treatment. Single-cell analysis identified fewer Ero1a+Bnip3+ macrophages and more C1qa+C1qb+ macrophages. These changes were accompanied by differences in maturation- and phagocytosis-related signatures. Neutrophil-associated transcriptional programs and inferred CCL, CXCL, MIF, TNF, complement, and galectin signaling also differed between groups. CONCLUSION: Untargeted metabolomic profiling identified lower hepatic 3-IAA abundance after IRI, and pretreatment with exogenous 3-IAA attenuated liver injury in mice. Protection was associated with changes in macrophage and neutrophil abundance, cell states, and inferred immune communication.

articles.title: Ceftazidime-avibactam monotherapy versus combination therapy for carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacterial infections: a secondary meta-analysis of predominantly critically ill cohorts.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative bacterial (CR-GNB) infections pose a critical threat to global public health, particularly in critically ill patients where treatment options are severely limited. Ceftazidime-avibactam (CAZ/AVI) is a novel β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor combination that has become a cornerstone therapy, yet its optimal use-as monotherapy or in combination with other agents-remains debated. OBJECTIVE: To systematically evaluate the comparative efficacy, renal safety, and risk of on-treatment resistance emergence between CAZ/AVI monotherapy and combination therapy in adult patients with confirmed CR-GNB infections. Because individual-patient data were unavailable, pooled estimates are derived from mixed cohorts in which approximately 82% of participants were ICU-admitted critically ill patients (critically ill is defined as intensive care unit admission or APACHE II score ≥15). METHODS: This study is a secondary reanalysis of the aggregate dataset compiled by Hsu et al. (2024); no de novo systematic search was performed. Studies comparing CAZ/AVI monotherapy versus any combination regimen for the treatment of CR-GNB infections were eligible. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. The secondary outcomes included in-hospital, 14-day, and 90-day mortality; clinical cure; microbiological eradication; acute kidney injury (AKI); and on-treatment resistance emergence. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. The heterogeneity was assessed via I2 statistics, and publication bias was evaluated using funnel plots and Egger's test. Subgroup analyses were prespecified by pathogen type, infection site, combination regimen, geographic region, and study design. RESULTS: Twenty-five studies (23 retrospective cohorts and two prospective cohorts) enrolling 2,676 patients were included. The pooled 30-day mortality was 31.2% in the combination group and 32.8% in the monotherapy group, with no significant difference (RR = 0.91, 95% CI 0.79-1.04, P = 0.17; I2 = 34%). In-hospital mortality (RR = 1.00, 95% CI 0.78-1.27), 14-day mortality (RR = 1.54, 95% CI 0.26-9.28), and 90-day mortality (RR = 1.18, 95% CI 0.64-2.18) showed no significant between-group differences. Clinical cure rates were comparable (RR = 0.95, 95% CI 0.84-1.08; I2 = 39%). Microbiological eradication did not differ significantly between groups (RR = 1.15, 95% CI 1.00-1.33; P = 0.05; I2 = 31%). AKI incidence did not differ overall (RR = 0.92, 95% CI 0.69-1.22; I2 = 42%), although a post hoc analysis showed a non-statistically significant trend toward higher nephrotoxicity for polymyxin-containing combination regimens (RR = 1.28, 95% CI 0.94-1.74). On-treatment resistance emergence did not differ significantly between groups (RR = 0.71, 95% CI 0.42-1.21; P = 0.21; I2 = 19%). Subgroup analyses consistently showed no mortality benefit across pathogen types, infection sites, or specific combination agents. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the findings, and no significant publication bias was detected. CONCLUSION: This secondary meta-analysis, based on the aggregate dataset compiled by Hsu et al. (2024), suggests that CAZ/AVI combination therapy does not confer a statistically significant survival or clinical cure advantage over monotherapy in patients with CR-GNB infections, although it was associated with a non-significant trend toward higher microbiological eradication and lower on-treatment resistance emergence. Given the predominantly observational nature of the included studies, high-quality randomized controlled trials are urgently warranted to guide clinical decision-making. Until higher-certainty evidence becomes available, these very-low-certainty findings support cautious, individualized decision-making: CAZ/AVI monotherapy may be a reasonable default therapeutic option for many patients, whereas combination therapy could be considered in selected high-risk scenarios, carefully balancing the unproven microbiological signals against increased toxicity and cost.

articles.title: Traditional Chinese Medicine Ameliorates Ulcerative Colitis Through Multi-target Regulation of the NLRP3 Inflammasome: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: In traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), ulcerative colitis (UC)-like manifestations are commonly related to diarrhea, dysentery, chronic dysentery, and hematochezia. Classical prescriptions and medicinal materials used for these conditions are increasingly investigated for their capacity to regulate the NLRP3 inflammasome, a central inflammatory platform in UC. AIM OF THE STUDY: This review aims to elucidate the regulatory mechanisms of the NLRP3 inflammasome in the pathophysiology of UC and to systematically analyze the pharmacological mechanisms underlying TCM-mediated modulation of the NLRP3 inflammasome for UC amelioration. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Web of Science, PubMed, Embase, and MEDLINE were searched using the combined keywords "NLRP3 inflammasome," "traditional Chinese medicine," and "ulcerative colitis" and relevant intervention names. A systematic review was conducted on animal and cell studies that met the criteria. RESULTS: The available evidence indicates that TCM interventions can attenuate NLRP3 activation and downstream Caspase-1/GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis, enhance autophagy and mitophagy, regulate gut microbiota-derived metabolites, reduce mitochondrial oxidative stress, and influence upstream pathways including NF-κB, TLR4/MyD88, TXNIP, AMPK/ULK1, PINK1/Parkin, AhR, and Nrf2. However, most evidence is preclinical; clinical confirmation, standardized preparations, exposure-response data, and rigorous safety assessment remain limited. CONCLUSIONS: TCM provides an ethnopharmacologically grounded source of multi-component interventions targeting the NLRP3-centered inflammatory network in UC. Future studies should directly connect traditional indications with authenticated botanical sources, standardized chemical profiles, clinically relevant dosing, and well-designed randomized trials.

articles.title: Precision drug delivery for ulcerative colitis: engineering the colonic microenvironment for site-specific and responsive therapy.
articles.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory bowel disease characterised by continuous inflammation and ulceration of the colonic mucosa, resulting from complex interactions among genetic susceptibility, environmental factors, intestinal barrier dysfunction, gut microbiota dysbiosis, and dysregulated immune responses. Although conventional therapies, including aminosalicylates, corticosteroids, immunomodulators, biologics, and small-molecule drugs have improved disease control, their clinical utility remains limited by incomplete therapeutic responses, adverse effects, loss of efficacy, and difficulties in achieving sustained remission. The present review offers an in-depth view of the emerging trends in molecular pharmacology and future drug-delivery systems for UC. UC-relevant molecular targets and pathological features of the colonic microenvironment be matched to site-specific or stimulus-responsive delivery strategies to improve local therapeutic exposure while limiting systemic toxicity, and clinical translation have been described. We discuss recent therapeutic advances targeting key inflammatory pathways (e.g. TNF-α, JAK-STAT, TYK2, IL-23/Th17, S1P receptors and PPAR-γ) and microbiome-directed approaches (e.g. faecal microbiota transplantation, microbial metabolites and postbiotics). Biomarker-driven approaches, such as faecal calprotectin and microbiota profiling, are emphasised as key components of precision medicine and treatment monitoring. Advanced Drug delivery mechanisms such as liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, solid lipid nanoparticles, hydrogels, microparticles, nanogels and multifunctional theranostic systems provide opportunities for colon-specific drug delivery, controlled release, improved bioavailability, improved mucosal targeting and decreased systemic exposure. New approaches based on RNA-based therapeutics, CRISPR/Cas technologies and artificial intelligence-assisted drug delivery system design further increase the possibilities of personalised treatment. To summarise, the combination of molecularly targeted pharmacology with intelligent and site-specific drug-delivery technologies is an exciting avenue for enhancing therapeutic efficacy and reducing treatment-related toxicity and for furthering personalised management of UC. However, translation to widespread clinical practice will need to overcome challenges related to biocompatibility, gastrointestinal variability, scalability, manufacturing, controlled release, and regulatory approval.

articles.title: Hydrogel-based drug delivery systems for the synergistic regulation of angiogenesis and osteogenesis.
articles.abstract: Bone defect repair remains a major challenge in clinical treatment, and insufficient vascularization is an important factor limiting bone regeneration. Owing to their favorable biocompatibility, extracellular matrix-mimicking three-dimensional network structures, and tunable degradation and drug release properties, hydrogels can encapsulate and locally release bioactive agents that promote angiogenesis and osteogenesis, providing a promising drug delivery platform for the coordinated regulation of angiogenesis and bone regeneration. This review comprehensively summarizes the applications of hydrogel-based drug delivery systems in the coordinated regulation of angiogenesis and osteogenesis during bone regeneration. First, we outline the biological mechanisms underlying angiogenesis-osteogenesis coupling. Second, we discuss passive controlled-release and active stimuli-responsive release strategies in hydrogels. Finally, we highlight the intrinsic relationships among the selection of therapeutic agents, drug release, and regenerative repair outcomes, while summarizing current challenges and future research directions. This review provides insights into the rational design of hydrogel-based therapeutic systems for vascularized bone regeneration and contributes to advancing research and development in this field.

articles.title: From prediction to functional delivery: evaluating artificial intelligence in lipid nanoparticle design.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is expanding the chemical and formulation space explored for nucleic acid lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), but accurate assay prediction does not by itself establish useful delivery in vivo. This critical narrative review examines how evidence links molecular design, complete formulation identity, and biological context to cell-resolved function, with a focus on mRNA. We distinguish tissue accumulation from functional cargo delivery, membrane damage from productive release, and target-cell coverage from panel-restricted on-target precision. Four purposively selected cases illustrate distinct inference problems: AGILE's selected-candidate association and reformulation, Hamilton's non-AI accumulation screen and functional follow-up, LANTERN's benchmark using AGILE-derived data, and Wang's delivery-classification and pKa-regression workflow with changes between screening rounds. We propose a claim-specific evidence audit and a prospective comparison whose primary outcome is the number of confirmed qualifying formulations found within a declared resource ceiling. Manufacturing, storage, and tolerability are considered where they constrain the application. Neither the audit nor the comparison design has been empirically validated. They identify testable requirements for evaluating whether AI improves a declared delivery decision.

articles.title: From direct inhibition to induced degradation: clinical progress of MCL-1-targeted interventions in cancer.
articles.abstract: MCL-1 is the most widely expressed and most rapidly turned over pro-survival member of the BCL-2 family, and the survival of acute myeloid leukemia, multiple myeloma, and many solid tumors depends at least in part on this protein. Several MCL-1-selective inhibitors have entered clinical trials; however, because cardiomyocytes also depend on MCL-1 for survival, direct inhibition has a structurally narrow therapeutic window, single-agent activity has been modest, and no inhibitor has been approved to date. In recent years, the research focus of MCL-1 targeting has shifted from direct occupancy toward downregulation and degradation. CDK9/BET transcriptional inhibition, translational and signaling interventions, pro-ubiquitination, and PROTACs and molecular glues lower MCL-1 within hours and reverse venetoclax resistance, although no degrader has yet entered a registered trial. At present, MCL-1 intervention is positioned mainly as a combination and sequencing component in resistant disease; response prediction relies on dynamic BH3 profiling, and cardiac safety monitoring is a common prerequisite across all routes. Looking forward, the first clinical validation of the degradation paradigm and biomarker-driven patient selection will determine the clinical prospects of this target.

articles.title: SENP3 loss in biliary tract cancer chemoresistance: substrate-specific control of fatty acid oxidation and mitophagy.
articles.abstract: Chemoresistance limits the benefit of first-line therapy in advanced biliary tract cancer (BTC); the mechanisms reviewed here were identified in models of acquired resistance to gemcitabine, a core component of combination regimens. Recent studies implicate loss of small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO)-specific peptidase 3 (SENP3) in gemcitabine resistance through distinct upstream routes: METTL3-mediated N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification and YTHDF2-dependent decay of SENP3 mRNA in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC), and increased proteasomal degradation of SENP3 in gemcitabine-resistant gallbladder cancer (GBC) cells with reduced reactive oxygen species (ROS). In ICC models, SENP3 loss promotes stabilization of hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase trifunctional multienzyme complex subunit alpha (HADHA) through proposed SUMOylation-ubiquitination crosstalk involving K309 and K531, accompanied by enhanced fatty acid oxidation (FAO) and lipophagy-associated lipid mobilization. Trimetazidine attenuates the resistant phenotype in preclinical models, although HADHA-specific drug action has not been established. In GBC models, SENP3 loss increases SUMOylation of Reptin (RUVBL2) at K456, redirecting Reptin to the nucleus, where it upregulates PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1) and sustains a mitophagy-ROS feedback loop. CB-6644, an RUVBL1/2 ATPase inhibitor, enhances gemcitabine sensitivity and suppresses PINK1-associated mitophagy in GBC cells; the combination also showed antitumor activity in xenograft models, without establishing specific inhibition of Reptin K456 SUMOylation. This cross-substrate comparison reveals distinct protein-stability and subcellular-localization outcomes downstream of SENP3 loss and identifies substrate selectivity, potential FAO-mitophagy interactions, and clinical predictive utility as key questions for future investigation. Whether the two mechanisms coexist or interact within the same tumor remains untested.

articles.title: Targeting MicroRNAs in the perioperative window to prevent surgery-induced metastasis and postoperative cancer recurrence.
articles.abstract: Surgery remains a central curative treatment for many solid tumors; however, postoperative recurrence and distant metastasis continue to limit long-term survival. The perioperative period is increasingly recognised as a biologically active window during which surgical trauma, inflammation, wound repair, hypoxia, platelet activation, immunosuppression, anaesthetic exposure, and extracellular vesicle signalling may influence the survival and outgrowth of residual tumour cells, circulating tumour cells, and dormant micrometastases. MicroRNAs are particularly relevant in this context because they regulate coordinated gene networks involved in tumor survival, epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity, angiogenesis, immune escape, and metastatic niche formation. OncomiRs such as miR-21, miR-10b, miR-155, miR-210, and miR-221/222 may promote recurrence-associated signaling, whereas tumor-suppressive miRNAs including miR-34a, the miR-200 family, let-7, miR-126, miR-143/145, and miR-29 may restrict metastatic progression. This review provides a translational framework linking surgery-induced host responses with miRNA-mediated metastatic regulation. It discusses perioperative immune and stromal remodeling, anesthetic and analgesic influences, exosomal miRNAs, biomarker-guided monitoring, therapeutic delivery systems, safety concerns, and clinical trial design. Although perioperative miRNA therapy is not yet a validated clinical intervention, serial miRNA profiling combined with ctDNA, circulating tumor cells, cytokines, and clinicopathological variables may support future precision strategies to identify high-risk patients and guide recurrence-prevention studies. The key challenge is to suppress pro-metastatic signaling without impairing wound healing, infection control, or postoperative recovery.

articles.title: The next frontier of peptide therapeutics: from targeted conjugates (PDC/ODC) to AI-driven safety-by-design.
articles.abstract: The pharmaceutical landscape is witnessing a profound "Peptide Renaissance," driven primarily by the clinical success of GLP-1 receptor agonists and reinforced by engineering advanced drug delivery platforms. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of current trends in peptide-based drug development, using a target-localization framework that distinguishes molecular recognition from pharmacological action. We delineate the functional divergence between extracellular, cell-surface, and intracellular targeting, highlighting how peptides bridge the gap between small molecules and monoclonal antibodies. Central to this discussion is a comparative evaluation of next-generation conjugation technologies-Peptide-Drug Conjugates (PDCs) and Oligonucleotide-Drug Conjugates (ODCs)-against the backdrop of conventional Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs). Rather than a simple performance comparison, this analysis focuses on how the distinct structural architectures of these modalities dictate their pharmacological profiles. We examine the inherent trade-offs between the long systemic half-life of bulky, antibody-based scaffolds and the construct-dependent tissue distribution and immunogenicity of peptide and oligonucleotide delivery systems, thereby elucidating their respective strengths and limitations in targeting complex disease environments. PDCs can use peptide-mediated recognition or uptake to deliver therapeutic payloads, whereas ODCs deliver oligonucleotides that act intracellularly through mechanisms such as RNA interference or splice modulation. Furthermore, we explore the transformative role of generative Artificial Intelligence and structural algorithms, such as AlphaFold 3, in shifting the development paradigm toward a "Safety-by-Design" philosophy. By integrating predictive toxicology (e.g., pepADMET) into the nascent design phase, researchers may prioritize candidates for experimental testing. Importantly, the pharmacoeconomic case for this approach remains provisional rather than established. A retrospective analysis of AI-derived candidates reported Phase I success rates of approximately 80%-90% and a Phase II success rate of approximately 40%, comparable to historical Phase II averages. The limited sample and historical comparison do not establish a causal effect of AI or a peptide-specific economic benefit. We therefore present AI-guided safety-by-design as a proposed strategy for candidate prioritization, and set out explicitly the comparative evidence that would be required before claims of reduced development cost, shortened timelines, or improved affordability can be regarded as demonstrated.

articles.title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals cellular atlases and cell-cell interaction networks in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To summarize recent advances in single-cell multi-omics technologies in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), with a focus on cellular atlases, cellular heterogeneity, and intercellular communication networks in hepatic and extrahepatic tissues. METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes findings from studies identified primarily through PubMed searches supplemented by manual curation of reference lists. Search terms included "single-cell," "spatial transcriptomics," "MASLD," "NAFLD," "NASH," "MASH," "steatohepatitis," and "liver fibrosis." Studies applying single-cell transcriptomics, single-nucleus RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, single-cell eQTL analysis, and integrative multi-omics approaches were included. The last literature search was conducted in July 2026. Results: Single-cell technologies have revealed key cellular alterations during MASLD progression, including disrupted hepatocyte metabolic zonation, heterogeneous activation states of hepatic stellate cells, macrophage functional reprogramming, immune cell dysfunction, and dynamic remodeling of the hepatic microenvironment. Spatial transcriptomics has further resolved the spatial organization of these cellular changes, whereas single-cell eQTL analyses have linked genetic susceptibility loci to cell-specific regulatory programs. Single-cell profiling of intestinal, adipose, and vascular tissues has expanded the understanding of extrahepatic contributions and gut-liver communication in MASLD. These advances provide a foundation for drug target identification, mechanistic understanding of current and investigational therapies, and assessment of treatment response at cellular resolution. CONCLUSION: Single-cell multi-omics is transforming MASLD research from tissue-level characterization toward cellular-resolution understanding, providing novel insights into disease stratification, therapeutic target discovery, and biomarker development, and advancing precision hepatology.

articles.title: A pilot randomized feasibility trial of perioperative melatonin for cardiac arrhythmias during CPB weaning, sedative and analgesic medication use, and mechanical ventilation following CABG.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Perioperative complications remain common following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Although melatonin may have cardioprotective and sedative-sparing effects, its feasibility and potential effects on early postoperative cardiac rhythm and recovery in patients undergoing CABG remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: To assess the feasibility of a future definitive randomized controlled trial (RCT) of perioperative melatonin in patients undergoing on-pump CABG and to obtain preliminary estimates of its effects on cardiac arrhythmias during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) weaning, duration of mechanical ventilation, and postoperative sedative and analgesic medication use. METHODS: In this pilot randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled feasibility trial, 22 adults undergoing elective on-pump CABG were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive oral melatonin (3 mg) or placebo nightly, from three nights before to three nights after surgery. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, retention, protocol adherence, completeness of outcome assessment, and intervention safety. Exploratory clinical outcomes included cardiac arrhythmias during CPB weaning, duration of mechanical ventilation, and postoperative sedative and analgesic medication use. RESULTS: Twenty-two participants were randomized. The recruitment rate was 68.75%, while retention, protocol adherence, and completeness of outcome assessment were all 100%; no treatment-related adverse events were observed. Arrhythmias during CPB weaning occurred in 2 of 11 participants (18.2%) in each group (OR, 1.00; 95% CI: 0.11-8.73). The median duration of mechanical ventilation was 9.5 hours with melatonin and 15.0 hours with placebo (Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the between-group location shift, -3.30 hours; 95% CI: -6.90 to 1.05). Postoperative sedative and analgesic medication use was generally comparable between groups, although the corresponding effect estimates were imprecise. CONCLUSION: Melatonin was feasible and well tolerated in this pilot cohort, with no treatment-related adverse events observed. The exploratory estimates were imprecise and do not provide evidence of efficacy, supporting a larger, adequately powered randomized trial to further evaluate the efficacy and safety of melatonin. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: IRCT20250206064666N1, date of registration: 2025-02-24.

articles.title: Changes in the color of azulene derivative-excipient mixed powders: Evaluation of the causes.
articles.abstract: The color of drug products is a critical characteristic that affects product quality and commercial value. Herein, mixed powders of sodium guaiazulene sulfonate hydrate (SGH) and nine pharmaceutical excipients were prepared and stored under different relative humidity (RH) conditions. The factors causing changes in the color of the mixed powders were investigated based on moisture content and drug content measurements. The SGH-excipient intermolecular interactions were also evaluated using Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. Pronounced color changes were observed in mixed powders containing polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), citric acid (CA), xylitol (XYL), and sorbitol (SRB) at high RH. In SGH-PVP, the color changes were associated with SGH dissolution due to moisture absorption into PVP, whereas those in SGH-CA were associated with SGH degradation. In contrast, no decrease in the SGH content was observed in the SGH-XYL or SGH-SRB mixed powders. FTIR analysis suggested intermolecular interactions of the double bonds and the sulfonate groups of SGH with the hydroxyl groups of sugar alcohols, indicating that intermolecular interactions contributed to the color changes. These findings suggest that color changes are associated with SGH degradation, moisture-induced changes in SGH, and intermolecular interactions of SGH with excipients.

articles.title: Mitigating artificial oxidation during liquid chromatography fractionation of therapeutic proteins.
articles.abstract: Therapeutic proteins are inherently heterogeneous, necessitating chromatographic separation of individual variants for in-depth characterization. However, conventional liquid chromatography (LC) fractionation can introduce artificial oxidation via UV exposure in the detector, confounding the analysis of critical quality attributes (CQAs). Here we describe a new cation-exchange HPLC (CEX-HPLC) fractionation method that incorporates methionine as an in-line oxidation scavenger throughout the process. This approach significantly reduces UV-induced oxidation artifacts, enabling accurate characterization of oxidation-sensitive residues and preserving the biological activity of collected fractions. Using an IgG1 monoclonal antibody as a model, the methionine-supplemented fractionation dramatically suppressed complementarity-determining region (CDR) oxidation in the isolated fractions and preserved their binding potency relative to the conventional fractionation method.

articles.title: XuanYu TongJing Tang alleviates depressive-like behaviors in LPS-induced mice: involvement of PI3K-AKT and MAPK signaling pathways.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Depression is a severe neuropsychiatric disorder involving neuroinflammation and impaired neuroplasticity. XuanYu TongJing Tang (XYTJT) is a classical Chinese herbal formula documented in Fu Qingzhu Nvke. It was originally indicated for menstrual irregularities, chronic pelvic inflammatory disease, endometritis, and dysfunctional uterine bleeding, and it has also been applied clinically to mood disorders. However, whether XYTJT exerts direct antidepressant efficacy remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the antidepressant effects and molecular mechanisms of XYTJT using an integrated systems pharmacology approach. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The antidepressant efficacy of XYTJT was evaluated in mice with lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced depressive-like behaviors through behavioral tests, histopathology, and biochemical assays. Network pharmacology, transcriptomics-CMap analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations were employed to predict core targets and pathways, followed by experimental validation via Western blot and RT-qPCR. RESULTS: XYTJT pretreatment attenuated LPS-induced behavioral alterations, reduced hippocampal neuronal damage, elevated IL-10, and upregulated BDNF, TrkB, and PSD95. Notably, sucrose preference was not significantly altered among the groups. Network pharmacology identified 323 intersecting targets, with PIK3CA, AKT1, MAPK1, and MAPK3 enriched in PI3K-AKT and MAPK pathways, confirmed by transcriptomics-CMap. Benzoyloxypaeoniflorin, identified as a candidate neuroprotective component, showed concentration-dependent neuroprotection and stable binding to PI3K, AKT1, and MAPK3 in molecular dynamics simulations. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that XYTJT attenuates LPS-induced depressive-like behavioral alterations, potentially through modulation of the PI3K-AKT-GSK3β and MAPK-ERK-CREB1 axes and suppression of STAT3-mediated neuroinflammation. Further studies with pharmacological inhibitors or genetic approaches are needed to confirm causality.

articles.title: Repeated-dose oral safety assessment of Aucuba japonica extract in rats: hematological-splenic responses and reversibility.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Aucuba japonica Thunb. has been used traditionally in Korea and Japan as warmed, roasted, or mashed preparations applied topically to burns, incised wounds, chilblains, boils, and localized swelling. Traditional oral preparations of A. japonica have also been used for edema and cystitis. Despite these topical and oral uses, repeated-dose safety data for A. japonica leaf extracts remain limited. AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate repeated-dose oral toxicity, target-organ responses, and recovery following administration of A. japonica extract (AJE) in rats. MATERIALS AND METHODS: AJE was prepared from leaves and stems with 30% ethanol at 85°C for 3 h. Male and female Crl:CD(SD) rats received 0, 1,250, 2,500, or 5,000 mg/kg/day for 4 weeks, or 0, 625, 1,250, or 2,500 mg/kg/day for 13 weeks. Separate control and high-dose cohorts underwent 4 weeks of recovery. Hematology, clinical chemistry, organ weights, and histopathology were assessed. RESULTS: At 5,000 mg/kg/day for 4 weeks, reduced erythrocyte counts, marked reticulocytosis, splenic enlargement, increased spleen weight, congestion, and extramedullary hematopoiesis constituted an adverse hematological-splenic response. Hepatocellular hypertrophy was also observed. Findings at 2,500 mg/kg/day were treatment-related but considered non-adverse. After 13 weeks, 2,500 mg/kg/day increased male reticulocytes and produced predominantly minimal splenic congestion and extramedullary hematopoiesis in both sexes. Corresponding abnormalities were absent in separately designated recovery cohorts. CONCLUSIONS: Hematological-splenic alterations were the principal toxicity findings at high exposure. The integrated evaluation supported 2,500 mg/kg/day, the highest dose in the 13-week study, as its no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL). These conclusions apply to the tested AJE preparation.

articles.title: Honeysuckle extract attenuates lung ischemia-reperfusion injury: Involvement of TLR4/NF-κB signaling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Lung ischemia-reperfusion injury (LIRI) is the leading cause of primary graft dysfunction (PGD) after lung transplantation, with very limited targeted therapeutic options. Honeysuckle (Lonicera japonica Thunb.; Caprifoliaceae) is a classic traditional Chinese herbal medicine with heat-clearing and detoxifying effects, which has been widely applied to treat various pulmonary inflammatory diseases. However, its potential role in LIRI remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of honeysuckle extract against LIRI and explore the potential mechanisms underlying these effects. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The chemical constituents of honeysuckle extract were analyzed by ultra-high performance liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS/MS). Network pharmacology was utilized to predict its potential therapeutic targets and related signaling pathways. A BEAS-2B hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R) injury model and a rat LIRI model were established to evaluate the effects of honeysuckle extract pretreatment, and the levels of oxidative stress-related biomarkers and inflammatory cytokines were detected. Subsequently, techniques including quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), Western blotting, immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence were applied to verify its pulmonary protective mechanism, and transcriptomics and molecular docking were performed to provide exploratory evidence. RESULTS: A total of 91 constituents were preliminarily identified by UHPLC-MS/MS, mainly flavonoids, terpenoids and polyphenols. Network pharmacology predicted that TLR4/NF-κB was one of the core signaling pathways involved in LIRI. In H/R-stimulated BEAS-2B cells, honeysuckle extract improved cell viability, reduced intracellular oxidant-sensitive fluorescence and attenuated oxidative stress, restored antioxidant capacity, inhibited the production of pro-inflammatory mediators, and suppressed the activation of the TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB cascade. In LIRI model rats, honeysuckle pretreatment alleviated pulmonary edema and histopathological damage, restored pulmonary redox homeostasis, and decreased the levels of IL-6, IL-1β and TNF-α. Meanwhile, it downregulated the expression of TLR4 in lung tissues and reduced NF-κB p65-associated fluorescence intensity in lung tissues. Transcriptomic analysis identified 346 differentially expressed genes, which were significantly enriched in the Toll-like receptor, NF-κB signaling pathway and TNF signaling pathway. Molecular docking generated predicted poses and scores for morroniside and chlorogenic acid against TLR4-, MyD88-, and NF-κB p65-associated receptor models. These calculations do not demonstrate direct binding or establish which compounds account for the effects of the whole extract. CONCLUSION: In the experimental models used, honeysuckle extract pretreatment was associated with reduced indices of oxidative stress, inflammation, and lung tissue injury. Attenuated TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling accompanied these effects, but pathway dependence was not established. These findings support further evaluation of honeysuckle extract as a potential preconditioning intervention for LIRI.

articles.title: Multi-omics analysis links Lycium barbarum glycopeptide-mediated retinal protection to glycolytic remodeling and protein lactylation in retinitis pigmentosa models.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Lycium barbarum L. (goji, wolfberry) is a traditional Chinese medicinal and food plant long associated with nourishment and ocular health. Lycium barbarum glycopeptide (LbGP), a purified glycopeptide fraction derived from Lycium barbarum polysaccharides, has shown retinal and neuroprotective potential, but its metabolic mechanism in inherited retinal degeneration remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: To determine whether LbGP treatment is associated with glycolytic remodeling, lactate metabolism, and protein lactylation in experimental models of retinitis pigmentosa (RP). MATERIALS AND METHODS: Public single-cell RNA sequencing data from PRPF31-mutant and control human retinal organoids were integrated with retinal proteomic, lactylomic, and metabolomic datasets from wild-type, vehicle-treated rd10, and LbGP-treated rd10 mice. Findings were examined using lactate measurement, ATP detection, pan-lysine lactylation immunofluorescence, cell viability assays, Western blotting, retinal structural assessment, and dark-adapted electroretinography. RESULTS: PRPF31-mutant photoreceptors showed increased glycolysis- and hypoxia-related transcription with reduced phototransduction and oxidative phosphorylation. In rd10 retinas, LbGP treatment was associated with changes in glycolysis-related enzymes, disease-associated lysine lactylation, and energy-related metabolites. Integrated multi-omics analysis nominated a glycolysis-lactate-lactylation axis involving selected glycolytic enzymes and Kla sites. LbGP increased the viability of serum-deprived 661W cells and preserved retinal structure and function in rd10 mice. It also increased the lactate production in both 661W cells and rd10 retinas. The ATP levels, pan-lysine lactylation, and the expression of PFKP and LDHA were increased by LbGP treatment in serum-deprived 661W cells, with the effect partially blocked by HK1 inhibitor 2-DG. CONCLUSIONS: Glycolytic remodeling and protein lactylation may represent candidate mechanisms associated with LbGP-mediated retinal protection in RP models, supporting further pharmacological validation of LbGP as a Lycium barbarum-derived intervention for retinal degeneration.

articles.title: DNA-linked inhibitor antibody assay (DIANA): An advanced method for screening influenza endonuclease inhibitors.
articles.abstract: Influenza virus endonuclease cleaves host cell-capped RNA, an essential step in acquiring primers for initiation of viral transcription. Currently, one endonuclease inhibitor, baloxavir marboxil (marketed as Xofluza), is approved for clinical use, and others are under development. Development of new antivirals could be expedited by simple, cost-effective screening methods. We previously introduced a multiwell plate-based DNA-linked inhibitor antibody assay (DIANA) capable of detecting enzyme at femtomolar concentrations. DIANA has also been applied for high-throughput inhibitor screening, enabling determination of equilibrium inhibition constants (Ki) from single-well measurements. Here, we set out to extend DIANA to influenza endonuclease, to obtain standardized Ki values for a structurally diverse panel of known inhibitors and benchmark them against orthogonal assays, and to apply the resulting assay to a newly designed series of inhibitors built on a more synthetically accessible scaffold. To this end, we present the design and synthesis of an L-742,001 derivative linked to a reporter DNA oligonucleotide for use in DIANA. The endonuclease is captured by an immobilized antibody, and test compounds compete with the oligo-linked detection probe for binding to the enzyme, which is quantified by qPCR. DIANA was validated using a focused panel of influenza endonuclease inhibitors and benchmarked against AlphaScreen and differential scanning fluorimetry, with the three methods showing broadly consistent structure-activity relationship (SAR) trends. Finally, we designed, synthesized, and evaluated a focused library of hydroxypyrimidinone derivatives. The hydroxypyrimidinone scaffold retained potent endonuclease inhibition while offering a more synthetically accessible alternative to hydroxypyridinones, supporting its use for systematic SAR exploration.

articles.title: Effects of far-UV-C radiation on skin barrier related parameters of the stratum corneum using confocal Raman microspectroscopy.
articles.abstract: Far-UV-C irradiation has proven to be useful for eradication of multi resistant pathogens, while safe for the skin, as it induces only negligible amounts of DNA damage in the viable epidermis. Due to the strong absorption of wavelengths < 240 nm in the skin, the majority of light does not reach the viable epidermis, as it is absorbed in the stratum corneum (SC). Nevertheless, the SC plays an important part in the skin barrier function, and consequently, the question arises, if this can be affected by far-UV-C irradiation. Confocal Raman microspectroscopy was used to assess depth-dependent skin barrier function-related parameters within the human SC ex vivo following exposure to far-UV-C irradiation at 222 nm and 233 nm at bactericidal doses of 40 mJ/cm2. The lateral and lamellar organization of intercellular lipids, the water binding properties, the secondary and tertiary keratin folding properties, as well as concentration of natural moisturizing factors (NMF) were assessed. No disorganization of intercellular lipids in the SC was observed subsequent to far-UV-C irradiation, but for the control treatment of UV-A irradiation (lamellar organization) and application of 10% sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS, lateral organization). Similarly, the water binding properties determined by the weakly bound / strongly bound water ratio and keratin folding properties were not decreased after far-UV-C irradiation, but for control treatments. Therefore, based on the obtained results, an influence on the skin barrier function subsequent to 222 nm and 233 nm far-UV-C irradiation at 40 mW/cm2 cannot be inferred.

articles.title: Compatibility-governed spatiotemporal release of amphiphilic peptides from PLGA microspheres.
articles.abstract: Lipidated glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, such as semaglutide, achieve prolonged systemic exposure through reversible albumin binding. Further extending their delivery using PLGA microspheres requires understanding how peptide amphiphilicity influences transport within polymer matrices. Here, uniform-sized PLGA 50:50 and PLGA 75:25 microspheres with matched nominal molecular weights were compared using semaglutide as a model amphiphilic peptide. PLGA 75:25 microspheres showed faster early release and a more continuous release profile than PLGA 50:50 microspheres, despite the slower expected degradation of the higher-lactide polymer. Multiscale experimental and computational analyses linked this release inversion to physicochemical drug-polymer compatibility through primary-emulsion formation, peptide localization, and pore accessibility. Stronger peptide-polymer association with PLGA 50:50 was associated with smaller primary-emulsion droplets, greater emulsion stability, and preferential core retention, followed by restricted early pore accessibility and an erosion-associated secondary release phase. Conversely, weaker peptide-polymer association with PLGA 75:25 favored peripheral localization, earlier pore accessibility, and diffusion-dominated release. Extracted semaglutide retained its principal secondary-structure features, while core retention in PLGA 50:50 was associated with acid-related local spectral changes and a higher parent-referenced +58 Da modification-related signal. Both formulations produced sustained glucose-lowering effects in db/db mice, with PLGA 75:25 microspheres maintaining lower late-stage mean blood glucose levels. These findings establish a compatibility-guided framework connecting microsphere formation, spatial organization, release behavior, peptide chemical integrity, and in vivo pharmacological performance, highlighting the need to balance matrix retention with sustained delivery of amphiphilic peptides.

articles.title: Integrated Bioinformatics and Experimental Validation Reveal Cathepsin S and TGF-β1 of Microglia/Macrophages as Key Targets of Spinal Cord Injury Treatment.
articles.abstract: Spinal cord injury (SCI) is a severe neurological disorder that often leads to the loss of sensory and motor functions and may result in permanent paralysis. However, the key therapeutic targets for SCI remain unclear. In this study, we integrated hdWGCNA, machine learning, and network pharmacology analyses with scRNA-seq data to identify potential therapeutic targets for SCI, revealing cathepsin S (CTSS) and transforming growth factor-beta 1 (TGF-β1) in microglia/macrophages as key regulators of SCI therapy. Subsequently, we performed molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations of methylprednisolone (MP, a commonly used clinical drug for SCI) with CTSS and TGF-β1 to explore potential binding interactions as a hypothesis-generating approach. GO analysis revealed that both CTSS and TGF-β1 were enriched in biological processes related to the regulation of inflammatory responses, indicating their involvement in inflammation-associated pathways following SCI. And cell-cell communication analysis revealed the pivotal role of the TGF-β1 signaling network in both the autocrine/paracrine interactions among microglia/macrophages and the interaction between microglia/macrophages and fibroblasts, thereby attenuating neuroinflammatory responses and promoting tissue repair. Mechanistically, downregulation of CTSS and upregulation of TGF-β1 in microglia/macrophages are associated with attenuated polarization toward the pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype and improved motor function recovery in SCI mice. These findings highlight the pivotal roles of CTSS and TGF-β1 in counteracting neuroinflammation after SCI, which may serve as potential therapeutic targets for SCI, offering new avenues for precision treatment.

articles.title: Compound C6 accelerates chronic wound repair through FXR-dependent host responses and perturbation of staphylococcal arginine metabolism.
articles.abstract: Chronic and non-healing wounds remain a clinical challenge due to impaired tissue repair, persistent inflammation, and microbial infection. Compound C6 is a small-molecule farnesoid X receptor (FXR) agonist initially developed for fatty liver disease, but its effects on wound repair are unknown. Here, we evaluated the therapeutic potential of C6 in normal, diabetic, and methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA)-infected mouse wound models. Topical C6 accelerated wound closure, improved perfusion and vascularization, and reduced inflammatory cytokines. Mechanistically, C6 promoted endothelial migration and tube formation by upregulating VEGFA and eNOS, while suppressing macrophage inflammatory responses and NF-κB p65 phosphorylation. FXR silencing abolished these pro-angiogenic and anti-inflammatory effects, whereas FXR re-expression rescued them, and cellular thermal shift assays confirmed direct FXR engagement. In parallel, C6 directly inhibited S. aureus and MRSA growth, disrupted bacterial membranes, reduced biofilm formation, and exhibited a low propensity for resistance development. Transcriptomic and metabolic analyses revealed that C6 suppresses genes involved in arginine biosynthesis and catabolism, leading to reduced intracellular arginine. L-arginine supplementation partially restored bacterial viability. Crucially, we demonstrated that C6-induced arginine depletion occurs prior to detectable bacterial growth inhibition, establishing disrupted arginine metabolism as a primary cause of its antibacterial activity. Together, C6 promotes wound repair by coordinating FXR-dependent host vascular regeneration and inflammatory control with pathogen-directed antibacterial activity via arginine metabolic perturbation, supporting its further development for chronic and infected wounds.

articles.title: 4-O-(E)-Feruloyl-N-feruloyloctopamine suppresses mast cell-mediated allergic airway inflammation and pulmonary fibrosis.
articles.abstract: Previous studies demonstrated that ferulic acid exerts therapeutic effects on various inflammatory disorders, including arthritis, acute respiratory distress syndrome, and asthma. We synthesized a novel ferulic acid derivative (4-O-(E)-feruloyl-N-feruloyloctopamine, FOA), which has not been analyzed previously. We validated whether FOA modulates airway inflammation and fibrosis and unraveled its possible underlying mechanisms. In a murine model of ovalbumin (OVA)-induced airway inflammation, FOA treatment alleviated immune cell recruitment and reduced pro-inflammatory mediator and immunoglobulin (Ig) levels in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) and serum, respectively. In BALF and Lung tissue, pro-inflammatory cytokines were significantly suppressed by FOA treatment. FOA administration decreased the recruitment of mast cells into lung tissue and activation. We focused on FOA efficacy using mast cells, which are involved in asthma development. In RBL (rat basophilic leukemia)-2H3 and rat peritoneal mast cells (RPMCs), FOA pretreatment inhibited mast cell degranulation and pro-inflammatory cytokine production through intracellular signaling pathways, including Lyn, Syk, Akt, phosphoinositide 3-kinase, phospholipase Cγ, nuclear factor-κB, and MAPKs. To determine the pro-fibrotic function of activated mast cells, we stimulated mast cells for transforming growth factor-β expression and secretion, contributing to fibrotic symptoms in lung tissues. FOA administration suppressed these fibrotic symptoms. FOA pretreatment exerted anti-fibrotic effects in human lung epithelial cell lines (A549 and NCI-H358) through the suppression of fibrotic factor expression, and in a murine model of bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis. Collectively, our findings suggest that FOA may serve as a promising therapeutic candidate for allergic airway inflammation and pulmonary fibrosis.

articles.title: Targeting circCROT overcomes chemotherapy resistance through UPF1-TRPM2-dependent calcium-redox disruption in acute myeloid leukemia.
articles.abstract: Chemotherapy resistance is a major cause of relapse and treatment failure in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), yet the molecular mechanisms that enable leukemic cells to withstand chemotherapeutic stress remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified circCROT, a circular RNA derived from the carnitine O-octanoyltransferase (CROT) gene, as a regulator of chemotherapy resistance that is consistently upregulated in doxorubicin-resistant AML cells and relapsed AML samples. circCROT depletion promoted apoptosis and myeloid differentiation, induced cell-cycle arrest, and increased doxorubicin sensitivity in resistant AML cells and primary AML samples. Transcriptomic analyses revealed prominent alterations in ion transport- and redox-associated pathways following circCROT silencing. Mechanistically, circCROT interacted with UPF1 RNA helicase and ATPase (UPF1) and maintained expression of transient receptor potential cation channel subfamily M member 2 (TRPM2), a redox-sensitive Ca2+-permeable channel. circCROT depletion reduced TRPM2 expression and was accompanied by increased Fluo-4 fluorescence and reactive oxygen species levels, whereas UPF1 restoration partially reversed these changes. In vivo, lipid nanoparticle-mediated circCROT silencing enhanced the antileukemic efficacy of doxorubicin and reduced leukemic burden in xenograft and patient-derived xenograft models. Analysis of the BeatAML cohort further linked the UPF1-TRPM2 axis to ex vivo drug response and molecularly defined AML subgroups. Collectively, these findings indicate that circCROT contributes to the maintenance of chemotherapy resistance through the UPF1-TRPM2 axis and support circCROT targeting as a potential strategy to enhance chemotherapy response in AML.

articles.title: Boric acid attenuates bisphenol A-induced hepatorenal damage via modulation of lipid profile, inflammation, oxidative stress, and apoptosis: In vivo, in silico, and network pharmacological analysis.
articles.abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA) is a widely distributed endocrine-disrupting chemical associated with multi-organ toxicity through oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis. Boric acid (BA) has demonstrated antioxidant and cytoprotective potential in experimental models of chemically induced tissue injury. This study investigated BPA-induced hepatorenal toxicity and the potential protective effects of BA using integrated in vivo, molecular docking, and network pharmacology approaches. Forty-two male Wistar albino rats were randomly allocated into six groups (n = 7 per group): control (distilled water), vehicle (olive oil, 1.0 mL/kg/day), BA200 (200 mg/kg/day), BPA (130 mg/kg/day), BA100 + BPA (100 + 130 mg/kg/day), and BA200 + BPA (200 + 130 mg/kg/day). All treatments were administered orally by gavage for 28 consecutive days, with BA and BPA administered concurrently in the combination groups to evaluate the protective effects of BA during BPA exposure. The BPA dose was selected to establish an experimental model of hepatorenal toxicity rather than to simulate typical human environmental exposure. Serum biochemical markers of liver and kidney function, lipid profile, antioxidant enzyme activities, and inflammatory cytokines were assessed. Liver and kidney tissues were examined histopathologically and immunohistochemically for Bax, Bcl-2, caspase-3, and cytochrome c. Molecular docking explored predicted interactions of BPA and BA with superoxide dismutase (SOD) and catalase (CAT), while network pharmacology identified candidate molecular targets and enriched biological pathways. BPA exposure increased BUN, urea, creatinine, AST, ALT, ALP, total cholesterol, triglycerides, LDL-C, and pro-inflammatory mediators while reducing SOD, CAT, and GPx activities. Histopathological examination revealed necrotic changes, oedema, vascular congestion, inflammatory alterations, and changes in apoptosis-related immunoreactivity. BA co-treatment attenuated these alterations, with generally greater protection at 200 mg/kg. Molecular docking predicted potential binding interactions of BPA and BA with SOD and CAT; however, these predictions do not establish enzyme activation, inhibition, or a causal relationship with the antioxidant enzyme activities observed in vivo. Network pharmacology identified 31 overlapping genes associated with BPA, BA, and hepatorenal injury. JUN, STAT3, TP53, IL6, ESR1, EGFR, GAPDH, CCND1, HSP90AA1, and MTOR were identified as the ten principal hub genes, while functional enrichment highlighted pathways associated with inflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, and metabolic regulation. Overall, BA co-treatment attenuated BPA-induced hepatorenal injury under experimental toxicological conditions. The computational findings provide complementary, hypothesis-generating insights that require experimental validation. Further studies using chronic and environmentally relevant BPA exposure models are warranted to establish the translational relevance of these findings.

articles.title: Dietary steroidal lactone withaferin A targets thioredoxin reductase to promote apoptosis of TNBC in vitro and in vivo.
articles.abstract: Dysregulated activation of thioredoxin reductase (TrxR) is associated with tumor initiation and advancement, implying that TrxR-targeted inhibitors hold promise as anticancer therapeutics. Naturally occurring steroidal lactone withaferin A (WA) is a dietary bioactive phytochemical found in the medicinal plant Withania somnifera. It possesses potent anticancer properties. Here we show that WA may bind to the active center selenocysteine residue (Sec498) of TrxR and inhibit its activity. This inhibition disrupts the redox balance, leads to high levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS), reduced total glutathione and thiols content, which ultimately induces oxidative stress-mediated triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) cell apoptosis. WA treatment suppresses tumor growth in TNBC MDA-MB-231 xenografts. Overall, the identification of TrxR as a target of TNBC reveals a new mechanism underlying the action of this compound and advances its development as a chemotherapeutic agent for treating cancer.

articles.title: Genetically selected alcohol-preferring rats show increased heroin self-administration and upregulated VTA Oprm1 expression.
articles.abstract: Alcohol use disorder and opioid use disorder (OUD) are chronic relapsing conditions that share genetic and neurobiological substrates, particularly within mesolimbic circuits and opioid receptor signaling. Understanding their overlapping genetic vulnerabilities is crucial for developing translational models of cross-vulnerability. The Marchigian Sardinian alcohol-preferring (msP) rat line, selectively bred for high alcohol intake and preference, displays altered expression of stress- and opioid-related genes, including Oprm1, which encodes the μ-opioid receptor (MOP). However, Oprm1 expression and function in the ventral tegmental area (VTA), a key region mediating drug reinforcement, had not yet been characterized in this strain. Quantitative PCR revealed higher Oprm1 mRNA levels in the VTA of male msP rats compared to Wistars, while no difference was observed in females. Across two independent cohorts, male msP rats self-administered significantly more heroin than Wistar controls. To test causality between higher VTA Oprm1 expression and higher heroin self-administration, Oprm1 expression was downregulated in the VTA via shRNA, resulting in reduction of heroin self-administration over time with a larger effect in msP than Wistar rats. These findings indicate that elevated VTA Oprm1 expression contributes to the higher heroin self-administration observed in male msP rats. Given the lack of selectively bred lines for opioid preference, the msP strain offers a valuable genetic model for studying vulnerability to OUD and for exploring mechanisms underlying alcohol-opioid cross-vulnerability.

articles.title: MUG ChoSa1: A novel human chondrosarcoma model for preclinical evaluation of chemotherapeutics and carbon ion radiotherapy.
articles.abstract: Dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma is an aggressive bone malignancy characterised by intrinsic resistance to chemotherapy and radiotherapy, highlighting the need for representative preclinical models and novel therapeutic strategies. We established MUG ChoSa1, a patient-derived dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma cell line harbouring an IDH1 p.R132C mutation, and investigated its molecular response to carbon ion irradiation (C-ion IR), Doxorubicin, Lurbinectedin, and combination treatment. MUG ChoSa1 retained key morphological characteristics of the primary tumour, demonstrated stable in vitro growth and formed subcutaneous tumours in two NRG nude mice, providing preliminary evidence of its tumorigenic potential. C-ion IR induced dose-dependent G2/M arrest and rapid activation of the DNA damage response (DDR), including phosphorylation of ATM, ATR, CHK1/2, DNA-PKcs, and p53, with γH2AX induction but minimal apoptosis. Transcriptomic profiling identified 6852 differentially expressed genes after C-ion IR, characterised by downregulation of cell cycle regulators and enrichment of DNA repair, replication, checkpoint, and immune pathways. Both Doxorubicin and Lurbinectedin reduced cell viability, although Doxorubicin induced earlier and stronger apoptosis. RNA sequencing revealed distinct treatment-specific transcriptional programs, with Lurbinectedin preferentially regulating DNA repair, replication, and cell cycle pathways, whereas Doxorubicin predominantly activated stress-associated pathways. Combined Lurbinectedin and C-ion IR was associated with more pronounced transcriptional changes in DNA repair and replication-related programs, whereas Doxorubicin plus IR elicited a comparatively less extensive transcriptional response. RT-qPCR and immunoblotting supported treatment-associated alterations in DDR signalling. MUG ChoSa1 represents a clinically relevant model for dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma and demonstrates that C-ion IR induces a predominantly checkpoint- and repair-driven response that is differentially modulated by Doxorubicin and Lurbinectedin. These findings provide a molecular basis of further investigation of combination strategies involving C-ion IR, although their therapeutic efficacy remains to be established.

articles.title: Design and optimization of a nano‑transethosomes gel for dual delivery of diclofenac sodium and luteolin using a Box-Behnken approach for enhanced rheumatoid arthritis therapy.
articles.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis involves chronic autoimmune-driven synovial inflammation, oxidative stress, and joint degeneration. Luteolin (L) and diclofenac sodium (D) offer complementary anti-inflammatory effects, though each has limitations related to bioavailability or long-term safety. This study aimed to develop and optimise a transethosomal gel for the topical co-delivery of luteolin and diclofenac sodium to enhance dermal permeation and therapeutic efficacy. The formulation was optimised using an experimental design approach based on vesicle size, PDI, and entrapment efficiency. The optimised formulation (LD-TE-Opt) was incorporated into Carbopol 934-based gel and evaluated for physicochemical characteristics, in vitro drug release, ex vivo skin permeation, and pharmacological activity. The optimized system was incorporated into a gel and evaluated through physicochemical characterization along with in vitro and in vivo anti-arthritic assessments. Prepared transethosomes formulation presented vesicles size of 77.99 ± 0.62 nm, zeta potential - 38.3 mV, polydispersity index 0.2618 ± 0.002, entrapment efficiency of 80.44 ± 0.12% for luteolin, 76.37 ± 0.32% for diclofenac sodium, and in vitro release profiling of LD-TE-Opt was cumulative drug release: 85.04 ± 3.53% over 24 h. The optimized LD-TE-Opt formulation exhibited significant anti-arthritic activity, demonstrating greater efficacy than the diclofenac sodium. The LD-TE-OptG formulation demonstrated a thermal response time of 20.03 ± 0.15 s, indicating good analgesic activity. Further, LD-TE-OptG effectively reduced paw volume to 3.41 ± 0.03 mL by day 28, demonstrating significant anti-arthritic activity compared to the control and CFA-induced group. Luteolin-diclofenac co‑delivery produced a combined therapeutic effect anti‑arthritic response with limited toxicity, positioning the dual‑drug nanoformulation as a promising therapeutic horizon for rheumatoid arthritis.

articles.title: Effects of resveratrol and silymarin on behavior, serum monoamines, and oxidative status in a reserpine-induced model of depressive-like behavior.
articles.abstract: Depression is a complex neuropsychiatric disorder associated with emotional disturbances and cognitive impairment. In addition to alterations in monoaminergic systems, oxidative imbalance has been implicated in its pathophysiology. This study investigated the effects of resveratrol and silymarin, administered alone or in combination, on behavioral outcomes, serum monoamine concentrations, and systemic oxidative status in a reserpine-induced model of depressive-like behavior in rats. Fifty male Wistar rats were randomly assigned to five groups: control, reserpine, reserpine + resveratrol, reserpine + silymarin, and reserpine + resveratrol + silymarin (n = 10 per group). Depressive-like and anxiety-like behavior, locomotor activity, and memory retention were evaluated using the forced swim test, open field test, elevated plus maze, and passive avoidance test. Serum serotonin, dopamine, total antioxidant status (TAS), and total oxidant status (TOS) were measured to assess peripheral monoamine concentrations and systemic oxidative status. Reserpine produced marked behavioral alterations, including increased immobility, reduced locomotor and exploratory activity, increased anxiety-like behavior, and impaired memory retention. Resveratrol improved several behavioral outcomes, while silymarin produced improvements in selected measures. The combined treatment produced significant improvements in selected behavioral outcomes, with statistically greater effects than both monotherapies for selected measures. Significant group differences were also observed in serum serotonin, dopamine, TAS, and TOS. Resveratrol significantly increased serum dopamine and TAS compared with the reserpine group, whereas silymarin and combined treatment significantly increased serum serotonin. TAS was also significantly higher with combined treatment, while TOS was significantly lower in all treatment groups than in the Reserpine group. Resveratrol and silymarin improved several behavioral and peripheral biochemical changes associated with reserpine administration, although the extent of these effects differed across outcomes. The combined treatment produced greater improvements in some behavioral measures and was accompanied by a favorable systemic oxidative profile. Since the biochemical analyses were limited to serum, these findings should not be taken as evidence of changes in central neurotransmission or oxidative processes in the brain. Likewise, the greater effects observed with the combined treatment in some outcomes do not establish a synergistic interaction between resveratrol and silymarin.

articles.title: MechTox: an audited benchmark for ordinal drug-induced liver injury prediction with uncertainty and mechanism-oriented interpretation.
articles.abstract: Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) predictions are sensitive to cohort definition, molecular representation, model selection, and uncertainty assumptions. We developed MechTox as an audited benchmark/workflow for ordinal DILI concern prediction and reserve MechTox-NN for the dual-branch neural model. From a pool of 1,336 DILIrank source records, we resolved 1,216 compound identities, where 1,081 records had usable standardized structures, 674 had verified transcriptomic profiles, and 672 were dual-modal records; the primary three-class cohort comprised 512 compounds (147 vNo, 234 vLess, and 131 vMost), and 160 accepted ambiguous records were retained separately. The primary performance was evaluated through five repeats of five outer scaffold folds and five grouped inner folds. The pooled outer quadratic-weighted kappa (QWK) was 0.287 for Morgan fingerprint logistic regression, 0.232 for the ordinal RDKit descriptor model, 0.058 for late-average structure-pathway fusion, and 0.252 for MechTox-NN. A separate compound-bootstrap sensitivity based on repeat-averaged predictions resulted in a median QWK of 0.296 [0.207, 0.377] for MechTox-NN and was not treated as the confidence interval for the pooled estimate. The canonical single-sample gene-set enrichment analysis served as the primary pathway representation, and a custom signed rank-integral score was evaluated only as a sensitivity comparator. Source-shift cohorts and empirical prediction-set containment were used to characterize the behaviors under source composition changes and were interpreted descriptively. In the held-out permutation-calibrated mechanism analysis, cationic amine dealkylation alone met the family-wise support criterion; this finding was interpreted as an exploratory association.
