Thus, MechTox provides a documented uncertainty-aware framework for protocol-specific ordinal DILI benchmarking and mechanism-oriented hypothesis generation.

articles.title: Curcumin alleviates DSS-induced ileal pouchitis in rats and is associated with suppression of JAK2/STAT3 signaling.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Curcumin shows therapeutic promise for pouchitis; however, its underlying mechanisms remain largely unexplored. This study aimed to elucidate the protective effects and mechanisms of curcumin against ileal pouchitis in a rat model. METHODS: A rat model of ileal pouchitis was established and randomized into three groups: Group A (control), Group B (pouchitis), and Group C (curcumin-treated). We assessed general health, histopathology, inflammatory cytokine levels, and intestinal barrier protein expression. Fecal microbiota was profiled using 16S rRNA sequencing, and untargeted metabolomics was employed to identify differential metabolites. Integrative analysis correlated microbiota and metabolite profiles. Furthermore, network pharmacology predicted hub genes and pathways, which were subsequently validated through in vivo experiments. RESULTS: DSS induction significantly increased pro-inflammatory cytokines, which were suppressed by curcumin treatment. Curcumin also upregulated the intestinal barrier protein occludin. Microbiota analysis revealed that curcumin restored microbial diversity and increased the abundance of short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-producing beneficial bacteria. The microbial composition in the curcumin group (C) closely resembled that of the healthy control group (A). Metabolomic analysis identified phosphatidylcholine as a key differential metabolite elevated in the curcumin group. Network pharmacology identified STAT3 and JAK2 as central hub genes. Both mRNA and protein expression of STAT3 and JAK2 were significantly higher in the pouchitis group (B) compared to the control (A) and curcumin-treated (C) groups. CONCLUSION: Curcumin significantly ameliorates DSS-induced pouchitis by restoring intestinal barrier integrity, reversing microbial dysbiosis, and correcting metabolic disturbances. Its therapeutic effect is primarily mediated through the inhibition of STAT3 phosphorylation and downregulation of the JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway.

articles.title: Incomplete linkage disequilibrium between DPYD HapB3 variants: implications for pharmacogenetic phenotype assignment.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Reduced dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPD) activity is a major determinant of severe fluoropyrimidine-associated toxicity. The DPYD HapB3 haplotype is commonly identified through the synonymous variant c.1236G>A (rs56038477), which has traditionally been used as a proxy for the functional intronic variant c.1129-5923C>G (rs75017182). However, emerging evidence suggests that the linkage between these variants may not be absolute, potentially leading to inaccurate haplotype assignment. This study aimed to determine the frequency of clinically relevant DPYD variants in our population and to assess concordance between c.1236G>A and c.1129-5923C>G. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective observational study including 3276 individuals who underwent routine pharmacogenetic testing. Genotyping was performed using the OpenArray™ platform. Allele and genotype frequencies of clinically relevant DPYD variants were calculated, and concordance between c.1236G>A and c.1129-5923C>G was evaluated. Samples showing discordant or atypical HapB3-associated genotypes were subjected to confirmatory analysis by next-generation sequencing (NGS). RESULTS: Allele frequencies were consistent with those reported in European and Spanish populations. One biologically discordant genotype configuration was identified among 3276 individuals, in which c.1236G>A was detected in the absence of c.1129-5923C>G; this finding was confirmed by NGS. A second apparently discordant case, initially classified as homozygous for c.1129-5923C>G but heterozygous for c.1236G>A, was attributed to automated genotype misclassification by the Thermo Fisher Connect Platform. NGS analysis subsequently demonstrated homozygosity for both variants, whereas review of the cluster plot revealed atypical fluorescence patterns likely responsible for the erroneous automated genotype call. These findings indicate that, in our population, incomplete linkage disequilibrium between these variants, as well as technical limitations of genotyping platforms, may compromise accurate HapB3 characterization. CONCLUSION: Concordance between the HapB3-associated variants c.1236G>A and c.1129-5923C>G is extremely high but not absolute. Apparent HapB3 discordance may result from either rare biological dissociation or technical genotype misclassification, both of which can affect DPYD phenotype assignment. These findings support direct genotyping of c.1129-5923C>G whenever feasible and orthogonal confirmation of atypical or discordant genotyping results.

articles.title: Application of DASC and AUSC metrics in evaluating antimicrobial stewardship interventions in critically ill patients.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Conventional metrics reflect use volume, not spectrum breadth, limiting de-escalation assessment. Using days of antibiotic spectrum coverage (DASC) and antibiotic spectrum coverage use (AUSC), we applied a dual-dimensional framework stratified by restriction level to evaluate the impact of antimicrobial stewardship interventions on consumption and spectrum coverage in critically ill patients with infections. METHODS: In this single-centre retrospective before-after intensive care unit study, an antimicrobial stewardship program optimized prescribing and reduced broad-spectrum exposure. Antimicrobial use was stratified by restriction level and evaluated using conventional metrics, spectrum-based metrics and derived ratio metrics. RESULTS: A total of 200 patients were included, and baseline characteristics were comparable between the two groups. Among 200 patients (100 per period), median DDDs decreased from 26.25 to 17.90 (r = 0.223, 95% CI 0.087-0.351; P = 0.002), DOT from 24.00 to 14.00 days (r = 0.294, 95% CI 0.162-0.420; P < 0.001), and DASC from 219.50 to 135.00 (r = 0.290, 95% CI 0.156-0.413; P < 0.001). No statistically significant between-period differences were detected for AUD, AUSC, DASC/DOT, or AUSC/AUD. In the non-special-use stratum, DASC (114.50-63.50; r = 0.242, 95% CI 0.106-0.368; P < 0.001), AUD (99.87-87.24; r = 0.157, 95% CI 0.018-0.289; P = 0.027), and AUSC (923.93-761.25; r = 0.151, 95% CI 0.012-0.284; P = 0.033) were lower in the intervention period; no statistically significant differences were detected in the special-use stratum. AUD correlated with AUSC (Spearman ρ = 0.75), as did AUSC with DASC (ρ = 0.40; both P < 0.01). Length of stay was also shorter (median 15.00 vs. 11.00 days; P < 0.001) and cumulative use correlated with it (ρ = 0.74-0.79); after accounting for observation time, only the treatment-day rate remained significantly lower (adjusted IRR 0.834, 95% CI 0.736-0.944, P = 0.004). CONCLUSION: In this before-after study, cumulative DDDs, DOT, and DASC were lower during the intervention period, partly reflecting shorter length of stay. After adjustment, only the antibiotic treatment-day rate remained significantly lower, whereas DASC/DOT and AUSC/AUD were unchanged. DASC and AUSC may complement conventional metrics for describing spectrum exposure, but require further validation against prescribing appropriateness and clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Morusin induces GSDME-dependent pyroptosis in non-small cell lung cancer via the angiotensin II receptor type 2.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, its 5-year survival rate continues to be unsatisfactory. Current therapies are often limited by resistance, toxicity, or poor efficacy, highlighting the urgent need for novel strategies. METHOD: We performed a high-throughput compound screen for inducing cell death in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cells. Combined with lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release assays, cell death morphology observation, and propidium iodide (PI) staining, we confirmed the cell death mode as pyroptosis. Then, we conducted a genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screen to identify the critical regulator of compound-induced pyroptosis. RESULTS: The screening results showed that morusin is a trigger of gasdermin E (GSDME)-mediated pyroptosis in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cells. Importantly, morusin suppresses tumor growth in vivo. Through a genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screen, we further demonstrated that angiotensin II receptor type 2 (AGTR2) as a critical regulator of morusin-induced pyroptosis, acting via activation of the caspase-3-GSDME signaling cascade. Notably, morusin also upregulated AGTR2 expression in NSCLC cells. In an NSCLC mouse model, morusin treatment potently suppressed wild-type tumor growth, whereas its antitumor efficacy was substantially diminished in AGTR2-knockout tumors. CONCLUSION: Our study reveals a novel mechanism underlying the antitumor effect of morusin, establishes AGTR2 as a potential therapeutic target, and provides a rationale for pyroptosis-based therapy for NSCLC.

articles.title: Elsholtzia Bodinieri vaniot dichloromethane extract exerts anti-inflammatory effects in acute lung injury mice by regulating the CCR1 and FLT1.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a disease characterized by diffuse dysfunction leading to systemic inflammation, increased vascular permeability and loss of alveolar epithelial cell function. Elsholtzia bodinieri Vaniot is a traditional folk medicinal and edible plant endowed with heat-clearing(Qingre) and detoxifying efficacies. METHODS: The dichloromethane fraction of E. bodinieri Vaniot extract (EBED) was isolated and evaluated for anti-inflammatory activity. Chemical profiling of EBED was performed using untargeted metabolomics. Putative target genes of EBED were predicted through bioinformatics analysis, and the anti-inflammatory effects of EBED were assessed both in vitro and in vivo using a model of acute lung injury (ALI). Mechanistic validation focused on CC chemokine receptor 1 (CCR1)- and Fms-like tyrosine kinase 1 (FLT1)-mediated downstream signaling pathways by Western blot and inflammatory mediator detection. In addition, the impact of EBED on gut microbiota composition was evaluated in ALI mice via fecal microbiome analysis, with particular attention to changes in the relative abundances of specific bacterial genera. RESULTS: EBED exerted markedly superior anti-inflammatory activity compared with other fractions. A total of 1775 chemical metabolites were identified in EBED. Bioinformatics analysis predicted that CCR1 and FLT1 serve as potential target genes for EBED to exert anti-inflammatory activity against ALI, which was subsequently validated in inflammatory pathways. In vitro and in vivo experiments collectively demonstrated that EBED mitigates inflammatory responses via modulating CCR1 and FLT1, as well as their downstream signaling cascades including CCR1/Ca2+, FLT1/PRKCA and FLT1/PRKD2, thereby regulating the expression of inflammatory mediators. Furthermore, EBED remodeled the gut microbiota structure in ALI mice. Specifically, the abundances of beneficial bacteria including Akkermansia, Lactobacillus, Ruminococcus and Coriobacteriaceae_UCG-002 were markedly elevated, while those of harmful bacteria such as Rikenellaceae, Tyzzerella and Paraprevotella were distinctly decreased. CONCLUSION: In summary, the EBED demonstrates potent anti-inflammatory activity against ALI. This effect is mediated through the modulation of key target genes CCR1 and FLT1. Additionally, EBED exerts a favorable remodelling effect on the gut microbiota of ALI mice. These findings position EBED as a promising functional food ingredient and a potential therapeutic candidate for the prevention and treatment of ALI.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of datopotamab deruxtecan versus chemotherapy as a first-line treatment for patients with advanced triple-negative breast cancer.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The phase III TROPION-Breast02 trial demonstrated improved progression-free and overall survival with datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) versus chemotherapy in patients with previously untreated advanced triple-negative breast cancer who were ineligible for immunotherapy. This study evaluated the cost-effectiveness of Dato-DXd from the perspectives of the United States (U.S.) and Chinese healthcare systems. METHODS: A three-state partitioned survival model was developed using TROPION-Breast02 data, with a 10-year horizon and 21-day cycles. Costs and utilities were obtained from public databases and published literature. The primary outcome was the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER), expressed as cost per quality-adjusted life-year (QALY) gained. Willingness-to-pay thresholds were $150,000/QALY in the U.S. and $27,906/QALY in China. Sensitivity and scenario analyses assessed uncertainty and the robustness of the findings, and exploratory subgroup analyses were performed. RESULTS: Compared with chemotherapy, Dato-DXd increased costs by $565,572.29 and QALYs by 0.44 in the U.S., yielding an ICER of $1,287,001.65/QALY. In China, the corresponding increases were $39,052.50 and 0.42 QALYs, yielding an ICER of $92,640.82/QALY. Price reductions of approximately 62.43% in the U.S. and 28.83% in China were required to reach the respective cost-effectiveness thresholds. Progression-free survival utility and Dato-DXd price were the most influential parameters in one-way sensitivity analyses. In exploratory scenario analyses, limiting treatment duration to the reported median yielded cost-effective results in both countries. Assuming unchanged efficacy, a hypothetical reduction in the Dato-DXd dose from 6 to 4 mg/kg made it cost-effective in China but not in the U.S. Exploratory subgroup analyses yielded conclusions consistent with the base-case findings. CONCLUSION: At the modeled prices and under the base-case assumptions, Dato-DXd was not cost-effective compared with chemotherapy in either country. Price reductions could improve its cost-effectiveness. Results were sensitive to assumptions about treatment duration. The potential economic benefits of reduced-dose or fixed-duration strategies depend on clinical confirmation of maintained efficacy and acceptable safety.

articles.title: Protective effects of AKBA against hypoxia-induced cognitive dysfunction: potential involvement of SLC2A1, PTGS1, and BCL2L1.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Hypoxia-induced cognitive impairment (HICI) is associated with neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and gut microbiota dysbiosis, highlighting the need for effective neuroprotective interventions. Acetyl-11-keto-β-boswellic acid (AKBA), a bioactive triterpenoid derived from frankincense, possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, but its protective effects against hypoxia-associated cognitive dysfunction remain insufficiently understood. METHODS: This study investigated the neuroprotective potential of AKBA administered concurrently with hypoxic exposure and explored its associated molecular alterations. Network pharmacology, transcriptomic analysis, molecular similarity assessment, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were integrated to identify and prioritize candidate proteins. The protective effects of AKBA were subsequently evaluated in mice exposed to normobaric hypoxia (12.7% O2) for 10 days. RESULTS: AKBA administration attenuated hypoxia-associated cognitive deficits, accompanied by reduced inflammatory and oxidative stress markers, increased BDNF levels, decreased TUNEL-positive staining, and preservation of MBP immunoreactivity. These effects were associated with changes in cortical SLC2A1, PTGS1, and BCL2L1 expression, together with alterations in NF-κB- and Keap1/Nrf2-related protein levels. AKBA administration was also associated with changes in gut microbial composition, and exploratory correlation analyses suggested associations between selected bacterial taxa and cortical protein expression. CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings indicate that concurrent AKBA administration provides protection against hypoxia-associated cognitive dysfunction, potentially involving coordinated changes in inflammatory, antioxidant, and neurotrophic responses. However, the causal roles of the candidate proteins and gut microbiota alterations remain to be established through further functional investigations.

articles.title: Mechanisms involved in the sex-dependent dopaminergic neurodegeneration induced by MDMA in a mouse model of adolescent drug exposure.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA, or "ecstasy") is an amphetamine-related drug mainly used by adolescents. Studies in mice have demonstrated that MDMA administration induces toxic effects in the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system, some of which may be sex- and age-dependent. Since adolescence is a critical period for brain development, this study aimed to investigate some of the mechanisms underlying MDMA-induced toxicity in the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system of adolescent mice. METHODS: Male and female adolescent mice were treated with a regimen of MDMA (4 × 20 mg/kg, 2 h apart) that has previously been demonstrated to induce toxic effects in the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system. After treatment, mice were sacrificed at different time points (i.e., 30, 60 or 120 min) to evaluate loss of nigral dopaminergic neurons, antioxidant and proteasome activity, reactive radical species (RRS) and neurodegeneration-related proteins. Immunohistochemistry for tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) was performed in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc). Moreover, midbrains were evaluated for: i) activity of the antioxidant enzymes glutathione peroxidase (GPx) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) 1 and 2 of the proteolytic subunits β2 trypsin-like and β5 chymotrypsin-like of the proteasome system; ii) expression of SOD1 and SOD2 genes; iii) presence of RRS and iv) phosphorylation of the extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK1/2) and of the signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3). RESULTS: Male mice displayed: i) decreased TH immunoreactivity and cresyl violet staining (120 min after the last MDMA administration); ii) reduced activity of SOD and β2 trypsin-like proteasome subunit, both in basal conditions and 120 min after the last MDMA administration; iii) increase in p-ERK1/2 (30 min after the last MDMA administration). Female mice treated with MDMA displayed: i) decreased SOD1 and SOD2 gene expression and ii) increased GPx activity (both observed 120 min after the last MDMA administration). CONCLUSION: MDMA treatment during adolescence altered the homeostasis of the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system in both male and female mice. Adolescent male mice treated with MDMA appeared more sensitive to dysfunction in proteasome and ERK1/2 activation. Conversely, female mice efficiently maintained the antioxidant activity, which could contrast the neurotoxic effects of MDMA on the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system.

articles.title: Comparable TXNIP-inhibiting, anti-apoptotic and anti-diabetic effects of TIX100 and its individual enantiomers.
articles.abstract: Thioredoxin-interacting protein (TXNIP) is a stress-responsive gene that is upregulated by endoplasmic reticulum stress, cytokine toxicity and high glucose and pathologically elevated in diabetes. In pancreatic islets this leads to dysfunction and promotes beta cell apoptosis thereby contributing to disease progression. On the other hand, targeting inhibition of beta cell TXNIP has emerged as a promising, novel, therapeutic approach for type 1 diabetes. Indeed, genetic deletion or pharmacological inhibition of TXNIP protect against beta cell destruction and diabetes. TIX100 is an oral, small molecule TXNIP inhibitor currently completing Phase 1 clinical trials. Structurally, TIX100 is a chiral drug and thus far has been used as a racemate. Even though the effects of a racemate and its isolated enantiomers can vary greatly providing potential advantages for drug development, the properties of the individual TIX100 enantiomers have remained unknown. The aim of the current studies was therefore to elucidate how the individual TIX100 enantiomers compare to the TIX100 racemate. Using in vitro and in vivo studies in diabetic mice, we found that the TIX100 racemate and its individual R- and S-enantiomers are stable, have similar metabolic profiles and are comparable in potency and effectiveness of lowering beta cell TXNIP, promoting beta cell survival and function and protecting against beta cell destruction-induced diabetes. Taken together with the extensive preclinical work and the Phase 1 clinical trials using the TIX100 racemate that have not revealed any relevant safety concerns, no rationale for pursuing a single enantiomer for further diabetes drug development seems to exist in the case of TIX100.

articles.title: Diterpenoid tanshinones enhance CD8+ T-cell-mediated antitumor immunity in gastric cancer by suppressing ENO1 activity and glycolysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge contains bioactive tanshinones with antitumor activity, but whether diterpenoid tanshinones (DT) suppress gastric cancer by coupling glycolytic inhibition to CD8+ T-cell responses remains unclear. This study investigated the antitumor effects of DT and the contribution of the ENO1-lactate axis to tumor immune regulation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: DT composition was characterized by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry. Antitumor activity was evaluated in a subcutaneous syngeneic MFC gastric cancer model in 615 mice, including CD8+ T-cell depletion and lactate-challenge experiments. Tumor-infiltrating immune cells were analyzed by flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry, and multiplex immunofluorescence. In gastric cancer cells, lactate production and extracellular acidification were measured using colorimetric and Seahorse assays. Network pharmacology, drug affinity responsive target stability, and cellular thermal shift assays were used to identify and assess candidate targets, followed by western blotting and enzyme-activity assays. RESULTS: DT suppressed tumor growth and increased intratumoral CD8+ T-cell infiltration, whereas CD8+ T-cell depletion attenuated its antitumor effect. DT reduced lactate production and glycolytic activity in gastric cancer cells and tumors. DARTS and CETSA supported target engagement between DT and ENO1. DT reduced ENO1 enzymatic activity and phosphoenolpyruvate levels without markedly changing ENO1 protein abundance. Exogenous lactate promoted tumor growth, while acidic culture conditions reduced CD8+ T-cell viability. Compared with the model group, DT alone increased the percentages of CD8+ and GZMB + cells and decreased the percentage of PD-1+ cells in tumor tissue. CONCLUSION: DT restrains gastric tumor growth through an immunometabolic mechanism involving ENO1 inhibition, reduced glycolytic lactate production, and antitumor activity involving CD8+ T cells. These findings support further preclinical evaluation of DT and the ENO1-lactate axis in gastric cancer.

articles.title: Inhaled cannabis and oral alcohol: driving performance and subjective driving confidence in a human laboratory study.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Cannabis is the most commonly detected drug (second only to alcohol) among crash-involved drivers. Determining cannabis effects on driving performance is imperative to public health. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to assess a range of inhaled cannabis doses and an intoxicating dose of oral alcohol on simulated driving outcomes and subjective driving confidence. METHODS: Healthy participants who used cannabis (n = 9) were enrolled in this within-subject, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo-controlled, outpatient human laboratory study. Participants completed five experimental sessions to examine the effects of inhaled cannabis (0, 15, 30 mg THC; 15 mg THC + 7.5 mg CBD) and oral alcohol (0, 0.8 g/kg [15% less for women]). Data were collected at baseline and for 7.5 h after drug administration. RESULTS: Alcohol produced robust impairment on simulated driving performance outcomes (e.g., decreased lateral control; p<0.05). Cannabis decreased brake force and altered headway distance during obstacle navigation (p<0.05). All active doses of cannabis and alcohol decreased driving confidence (e.g., willingness to operate a real vehicle; p<0.05) and increased ratings of abuse potential (e.g., drug liking, p<0.05). High dose cannabis (30 mg) and alcohol increased subjective ratings of impairment and sedation (p<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Cannabis did not produce profound alcohol-like driving impairment; however, it was not without risk, and driving impairment was evident. All active cannabis doses decreased participants' driving confidence, while the highest dose of cannabis (30 mg) and alcohol increased self-reported impairment and sedation. Overall, even in a sample of near-daily cannabis users, cannabis negatively impacted driving performance, decreased driving acuity, and reduced confidence in safe driving ability.

articles.title: Long-acting targeted delivery of TNF-α-derived peptide for enhanced anti-renal fibrosis treatment via activation of the mitochondrial apoptosis pathway.
articles.abstract: Renal fibrosis is an excessive accumulation of the extracellular matrix in the kidney in response to injury, and thus leading to renal function loss, which lacks effective therapeutic agents in clinical settings. Herein, we engineered a multifunctional protein Z-IgBD-P16 derived from IgG-binding domain (IgBD) to extend the serum half-life and platelet-derived growth factor receptor β (PDGFRβ)-specific affibody ZPDGFRβ to enhance fibrotic kidney-targeted distribution of P16, an apoptosis-inducing TNF-α-derived peptide that specific binding to TNF-α receptor 1 (TNFR1) but not receptor 2 (TNFR2), as a model drug for renal fibrosis treatment. Z-IgBD-P16 possesses excellent targeting ability to myofibroblasts in TGF-β1-activated NIH3T3 cells and fibrotic kidneys in UUO mice. Z-IgBD-P16 also extends the serum half-life in the fibrotic kidney in the UUO mice model of renal fibrosis. Coupled with its high targeting specificity, the extended serum half-life of Z-IgBD-P16 confers sustained long-acting potential. Z-IgBD-P16 significantly mitigates renal fibrosis in in vitro cell and in vivo mice model of renal fibrosis by specific inducing myofibroblast apoptosis via the mitochondrial-dependent pathway. These findings suggest that Z-IgBD-P16 proves effective in treating renal fibrosis and warrants further investigation for its therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Market analysis of chondroitin and glucosamine as dietary supplements.
articles.abstract: Chondroitin and glucosamine are widely used as dietary supplements for osteoarthritis (OA), despite inconsistent clinical evidence and limited regulatory oversight. Concerns remain regarding efficacy, bioavailability, safety and discrepancies between marketed claims and scientific data. To investigate the characteristics of marketed chondroitin and glucosamine dietary supplements and to evaluate the clinical evidence regarding their efficacy and safety in OA. This study combined a cross-sectional market analysis of 110 dietary supplements with a structured review of clinical studies. Supplements were analyzed with respect to composition, dosage, pricing, labelling and marketing strategies. A PubMed search was conducted to identify clinical trials and meta-analyses investigating orally administered chondroitin and/or glucosamine in OA patients. Eligible studies were analyzed descriptively due to heterogeneity. The product analysis revealed highly variable pricing, with substantial cost differences and no clear link between price and clinical effectiveness. Marketing strategies often relied on packaging and presentation to imply scientific validation, frequently without sufficient supporting evidence. The available clinical evidence does not provide a consistent or robust basis for confirming the efficacy of chondroitin and glucosamine in OA. The effectiveness of chondroitin and glucosamine in OA in treating OA is questionable, a major problem being the poor bioavailability. Overall, the field is plagued by poor scientific evidence.

articles.title: From regulatory approval to patient access: A comparative analysis of biosimilar market entry timelines in Japan, the USA, and the EU.
articles.abstract: Biosimilar approval lag and biosimilar loss, the latter also referred to as the biosimilar void, remain important challenges particularly in Japan compared with the United States of America (USA) and the European Union (EU). However, regulatory approval does not necessarily translate into timely patient access. Although biosimilar approval lag has been widely discussed, international comparisons of patient access after regulatory approval remain limited. We evaluated biosimilar approval lag, market entry lag, and patient access time (defined as the interval between regulatory approval and first commercial launch). Commercial launch was used as the earliest measurable milestone of patient access, rather than as a measure of subsequent biosimilar uptake in clinical practice. Analyses were conducted using publicly available data from the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA), the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and the European Medicines Agency (EMA), supplemented by company press releases. The median patient access time was shortest in Japan (6 months) compared with the USA (15 months) and the EU (17 months). Despite a persistent approval lag, patient access to biosimilars in Japan was frequently comparable to, or earlier than, that in the USA and the EU, largely because of shorter approval-to-launch intervals. Regulatory approval timing alone is insufficient to assess patient access to biosimilars. Ensuring timely patient access requires a comprehensive approach that integrates post-approval pathways, including market entry, pricing, and reimbursement, with coordinated efforts across the full biosimilar lifecycle.

articles.title: Jujuboside A from Ziziphus: Chemistry, mechanistic pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, and formulation roadmap toward neuroactive translation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Jujuboside A (JuA) is a dammarane-type triterpenoid saponin and a principal quality marker of Ziziphi spinosae semen (ZSS) and selected Ziziphus taxa. OBJECTIVE: This review aimed to integrate current evidence on JuA chemistry, central nervous system (CNS) pharmacology, pharmacokinetics (PK), metabolism, safety, analytical standardization, and formulation strategies toward neuroactive translation. METHODS: Evidence relevant to these domains was synthesized and critically organized to define the chemical, pharmacological, pharmacokinetic, quality-control, and formulation profile of JuA. RESULTS: JuA is characterized by a jujubogenin aglycone linked to a branched oligosaccharide chain, while comparative Ziziphus saponins, including JuB, JuC, protojujubosides, and jujubogenin, clarify how glycosylation influences amphiphilicity, stability, and disposition. Mechanistic evidence is strongest for CNS-related effects, particularly GABAergic modulation, neuroinflammatory restraint, mitochondrial and synaptic protection, and sleep- or stress-linked behavioral outcomes. JuA shows low oral exposure, with an oral bioavailability of approximately 1.32% and rapid stepwise deglycosylation to JuB and jujubogenin, supporting a metabolite-driven pharmacodynamic model. Standardization should integrate authenticated botanical sourcing, ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) or charged-aerosol detection/quantitative nuclear magnetic resonance (CAD/qNMR) quantification, chemometric fingerprints, and contaminant controls. Lipid-based systems, cyclodextrin complexes, and amorphous solid dispersions should be evaluated for their capacity to protect labile glycosidic linkages, sustain supersaturation, and improve exposure to pharmacologically relevant species. CONCLUSION: Key priorities are direct receptor engagement, brain-region exposure mapping, PK/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) alignment, standardized clinical-grade materials, and early human studies using objective sleep endpoints.

articles.title: Recognition and management of semaglutide overdose and intoxi​cation: a narrative review for clinicians.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Semaglutide has moved within a few years from a niche glucose-lowering agent to one of the most widely dispensed medicines in high-income countries, and reported excessive exposures have risen in parallel. This review sets out a practical framework for recognising and managing semaglutide overdose, and distinguishes recommendations supported by published overdose evidence from those resting on pharmacological reasoning or general toxicology practice. EVIDENCE ACQUISITION: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase and Web of Science were searched from January 2005 to July 2026 for English-language human studies of semaglutide pharmacology, safety and excessive exposure, supplemented by reference lists and regulatory agency publications. Randomised trials and meta-analyses were prioritised for statements about incidence; case reports, case series and poison centre or pharmacovigilance analyses informed the description of the overdose syndrome itself. RESULTS: The dominant toxidrome is gastrointestinal and protracted, with nausea, repetitive vomiting, abdominal pain and anorexia persisting for days to weeks because the terminal elimination half-life approaches one week. Volume depletion, electrolyte derangement and acute kidney injury drive serious outcome. Hypoglycaemia is uncommon in isolated overdose because insulinotropic action is glucose-dependent, but it matters with concomitant insulin or sulfonylurea therapy, in non-diabetic individuals, and where a falsified product contains insulin. Pancreatitis, euglycaemic ketoacidosis, ileus and delayed gastric emptying with aspiration risk are less frequent but potentially life-threatening. In the cases reported to date, most exposures follow therapeutic error, unit-conversion confusion with compounded multi-dose vials, and acquisition outside regulated supply. CONCLUSION: Management is supportive and anticipatory. There is no antidote, and extracorporeal removal is futile given extensive albumin binding. Priorities are aggressive antiemesis, fluid and electrolyte correction, glucose monitoring proportionate to risk, full-stomach airway precautions, and observation that respects the drug's long half-life. Prevention through device design, dispensing standards, patient education and regulatory action is likely to yield greater benefit than any therapeutic manoeuvre.

articles.title: Small extracellular vesicle-associated miRNAs in lung cancer: therapeutic potential, drug delivery applications, and translational perspectives.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Small extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated microRNAs (miRNAs) have attracted interest as regulators of intercellular communication and candidates for lung cancer biomarkers and RNA therapeutics. However, uncertain cellular origin, analytical variability, and limited clinical validation complicate their translation. PURPOSE: To critically assess the biological functions, clinical applications, and translational readiness of EV-associated and exosome-enriched miRNAs in lung cancer. METHODS: A structured narrative review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science, covering publications from January 2017 to June 2026 and supplemented by foundational earlier studies. Evidence was purposively selected according to mechanistic relevance, methodological quality, clinical validation, and translational significance. Findings were synthesized using origin-confidence (OC1-OC3) and evidence-readiness (ER1-ER4) frameworks. RESULTS: EV-associated miRNAs were implicated in tumor-stromal communication, endothelial barrier disruption, metastasis, and treatment resistance. Of 11 patient-linked biomarker studies, ten analyzed total circulating EV fractions (OC1), while one used tumor-associated EV enrichment (OC2); patient samples did not verify a direct malignant-cell origin. Two diagnostic studies included independent external validation (ER3). Experimental studies supported EV-mediated transfer of gefitinib resistance-associated miR-214 and antimetastatic activity of miR-126-loaded EVs in vivo. Variability in EV isolation, hemolysis assessment, miRNA normalization, and clinical validation limited cross-study comparability. CONCLUSION: EV-associated miRNAs offer potential for lung cancer risk stratification, treatment monitoring, and therapeutic delivery. Clinical translation requires standardized vesicle characterization, independent prospective validation, and quantitative assessment of delivery efficiency, biodistribution, and safety.

articles.title: Chronopharmaceutics of In Situ Gel-Based Drug Delivery Systems in the Treatment of Nocturnal Asthma: Recent Advances, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nocturnal asthma (NA) is characterized by airway resistance and inflammation that peak between 02:00 and 06:00, driven by circadian fluctuations in vagal tone, cortisol, and inflammatory mediators. Conventional inhaled corticosteroid/long-acting β₂-agonist combinations and oral therapies may not reliably cover this window because of suboptimal adherence, heterogeneous lung deposition, and variable systemic exposure after oral dosing. In situ gels (ISGs), which are liquids that gel after administration, have been proposed as platforms for sustained nasal or pulmonary drug delivery. OBJECTIVE: To review the circadian mechanisms of NA, the formulation science of stimuli-responsive ISGs, and the evidence for their use as chronotherapeutic systems in NA. METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes literature on the molecular clock and circadian pathophysiology of asthma, polymer selection and gelation mechanisms, nasal and pulmonary delivery, pharmacokinetics and safety, and manufacturing and regulatory considerations. Evidence was classified by type (in vitro or ex vivo, animal, computational, or human) and as established, preclinical, or hypothetical. RESULTS: Thermosensitive poloxamers, pH-responsive carbopol/chitosan systems, ion-activated gellan gum, and enzyme-degradable matrices can form mucoadhesive depots, but their gelation behaviour, mechanical stability, mucociliary clearance, and tolerability depend on formulation composition and test conditions. Hybrid architectures (nanoparticle-embedded, nanomicelle-forming, and mesoporous silica ISGs) may allow release kinetics to be separated from cellular uptake. Sustained release over several hours has been shown for gel formulations in vitro. No study has evaluated a chronotherapeutic ISG in nocturnal asthma, and benefits for airway function and adherence remain undemonstrated. Afternoon or evening dosing of inhaled corticosteroids has clinical trial support and is the main alternative chronotherapeutic strategy. Data on repeated nightly dosing and on bronchial tissue drug levels after nasal administration are lacking. CONCLUSION: Chronotherapeutic ISGs are a plausible but untested approach to nocturnal asthma. Priorities for translation are studies that measure drug exposure across the 02:00-06:00 window, bronchial tissue drug levels after nasal administration, and the safety of repeated nightly dosing. Regulatory, manufacturing, biomarker-responsive, and digital-integration concepts remain exploratory.

articles.title: Pharmacological SIRT1 Inhibition Exacerbates Angiotensin II-Induced Myocardial Injury and Is Associated with Dysregulation of the p53-FOXO3a Stress-Response Axis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertensive myocardial injury is characterized by oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, and apoptosis, largely driven by the central effector angiotensin II (Ang II). Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1), an NAD+-dependent deacetylase, coordinates stress-adaptive signaling; however, the effects of pharmacological SIRT1 inhibition on Ang II-induced stress are not fully defined. OBJECTIVES: To determine whether SIRT1 inhibition exacerbates Ang II-induced myocardial injury and to delineate the associated redox and mitochondrial changes and SIRT1-associated p53-Forkhead box O3a (FOXO3a) signaling alterations in cardiac cells. METHODS: The primary outcome measures were cell viability, intracellular ROS accumulation, and mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm), selected to characterize the core injury phenotype induced by Ang II and its modification by pharmacological SIRT1 inhibition. Secondary outcome measures included apoptotic injury markers, specifically the PARP cleavage index, BAX, Bcl-2, and cleaved caspase-3, along with inflammatory transcript responses assessed by quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) of TNF-α, IL-6, and NF-κB. Exploratory mechanistic outcomes included acetyl-p53 immunoblotting and analysis of FOXO3a nuclear-cytoplasmic localization to examine potential involvement of the SIRT1-p53-FOXO3a stress-response axis. RESULTS: EX-527 significantly exacerbated the primary injury outcomes induced by Ang II, including reduced cell viability, increased ROS accumulation, and loss of mitochondrial membrane potential. Among the secondary outcomes, SIRT1 inhibition further increased the PARP cleavage index, enhanced BAX and cleaved caspase-3, suppressed Bcl-2, and augmented the Ang II-induced upregulation of inflammatory transcripts. Exploratory mechanistic analyses showed increased p53 acetylation and reduced nuclear enrichment of FOXO3a in the Ang II + EX-527 group, supporting involvement of the SIRT1-p53-FOXO3a axis in the aggravated injury phenotype. CONCLUSIONS: These pharmacological findings suggest that basal SIRT1 activity protects against Ang II-mediated myocardial injury by maintaining mitochondrial integrity and suppressing oxidative, apoptotic, and inflammatory cascades, with parallel changes in p53 acetylation and FOXO3a localization consistent with involvement of the p53-FOXO3a stress-response axis. However, causal validation of this pathway will require genetic and rescue-based studies. Pharmacological inhibition of SIRT1 aggravated Ang II-induced injury phenotypes in cardiac cell models, supporting SIRT1 activation as a potential therapeutic approach in hypertensive heart disease, although genetic validation remains required.

articles.title: Efficacy of Nanocurcumin in Preventing Paclitaxel-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy Among Breast Cancer Patients: Findings from a Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study evaluated the prophylactic efficacy of nanocurcumin in mitigating chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) among patients with non-metastatic breast cancer receiving paclitaxel. METHODS: In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial, 80 patients were enrolled after completing anthracycline- and paclitaxel-based chemotherapy regimens. Participants were randomly allocated to receive either nanocurcumin 40 mg twice daily or a matched placebo. The severity of CIPN was evaluated using standardized instruments, including the Neuropathy Disability Score (NDS), Neuropathy Symptom Score (NSS), and Michigan Neuropathy Screening Instrument (MNSI). Large-fiber neuropathy was confirmed by nerve conduction studies. Assessments were performed during the fourth and eighth weeks of the study. RESULTS: Sixty patients completed the trial, including 32 in the placebo group and 28 in the nanocurcumin group. Peripheral neuropathy indices, including NDS, NSS, and MNSI, improved significantly in the nanocurcumin group compared with the placebo group; however, no significant between-group difference was observed in the incidence of large-fiber neuropathy. In addition, nanocurcumin reduced symptoms such as fatigue and muscle cramps, based on NSS and MNSI findings. No adverse events leading to discontinuation were reported in either group. CONCLUSIONS: These results suggest that nanocurcumin may be a safe and potentially effective intervention for preventing paclitaxel-induced peripheral neuropathy in patients with breast cancer; however, further research is required to corroborate these findings.

articles.title: Adjunctive Nicorandil Ameliorates Cardiac Function and Clinical Outcomes Following Recombinant Human Pro-Urokinase Thrombolysis in Patients With Acute ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Recombinant human pro-urokinase (rhPro-UK) is a primary reperfusion strategy for acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). This study evaluated the clinical efficacy and safety of adjunctive nicorandil therapy alongside rhPro-UK intravenous thrombolysis in patients with STEMI. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the clinical application value of nicorandil combined with recombinant human prourokinase in patients with acute STEMI receiving intravenous thrombolysis. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 116 patients with STEMI (June 2024-March 2026). Patients were divided into a control group (rhPro-UK, n = 54) and an observation group (rhPro-UK plus nicorandil, n = 62). We compared reperfusion success rates, ST-segment resolution at 2 hours, and cardiac biomarker levels (cardiac troponin I [cTnI], creatine kinase-MB [CK-MB]) at baseline and 24 hours post-thrombolysis. Left ventricular function (left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF], left ventricular end-diastolic diameter [LVEDD]) was assessed on day 7. Clinical safety, including incidence of serious arrhythmias, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) within 30 days, and adverse drug reactions, was systematically monitored. RESULTS: The observation group achieved significantly higher rates of successful reperfusion (79.03% vs 61.11%) and ST-segment resolution (74.19% vs 55.56%) compared with the control group (P < .05). At 24 hours, the observation group exhibited lower cTnI and CK-MB levels and earlier peak CK-MB timing (P < .05). On day 7, patients treated with nicorandil showed superior LVEF and smaller LVEDD (P < .05). Furthermore, the observation group experienced fewer serious arrhythmias and lower 30-day MACE rates (P < .05). No significant difference in adverse drug reactions was observed between cohorts (P > .05). CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: Adjunctive nicorandil enhances the efficacy of rhPro-UK thrombolysis, mitigating myocardial injury and improving early cardiac function. This combination therapy reduces short-term cardiovascular risk without increasing adverse reactions, demonstrating favorable clinical safety and utility in STEMI management.

articles.title: CYP2C19 metabolizer phenotype and recurrent documented gastroesophageal reflux disease after proton pump inhibitor initiation: A cohort study from the All of Us Research Program.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: CYP2C19 influences proton pump inhibitor (PPI) exposure, but its association with longitudinal gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) documentation remains uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate associations between CYP2C19 phenotype and documented GERD outcomes after PPI initiation. METHODS: This retrospective All of Us cohort included 21,135 adults with GERD, a definitive CYP2C19 phenotype, and 365-day post-index observation. Recurrent documented GERD required at least 2 diagnosis dates occurring from day 31 to day 365 separated by at least 30 days. Modified Poisson regression estimated adjusted risk ratios (ARRs). A secondary composite assessed reflux testing or antireflux interventions. RESULTS: Recurrent documented GERD occurred in 5,927 participants (28.0%). Compared with normal metabolizers, ARRs (95% CI) were 1.11 (0.97-1.26) for poor, 1.02 (0.97-1.07) for intermediate, 1.04 (0.98-1.09) for rapid, and 0.97 (0.87-1.08) for ultrarapid metabolizers (global P = .353). Estimates were similar across alternative documentation definitions, ancestral alignment, and the restriction to omeprazole only. Among 20 928 secondary analysis participants, 245 (1.17%) underwent further reflux testing or intervention (global P = .679). Dose and ongoing exposure were not modeled. CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: CYP2C19 phenotype was not significantly associated with these documentation-based outcomes. This large genomic cohort extends evidence to longitudinal health care records, but exposure uncertainty and multifactorial GERD limit inferences about active treatment responses. The findings do not establish equivalence or justify changing genotype-guided dosing recommendations; clinical decisions should also consider dose, adherence, and the underlying symptom mechanisms.

articles.title: Combined effects of aerobic interval training and hesperidin supplementation on inflammatory and oxidative stress markers in a rat model of paclitaxel-induced neuropathy: evidence for additive therapeutic effects.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CINP) is characterized by numbness, pain, and motor dysfunction, primarily in the extremities. It is a common and debilitating side effect of paclitaxel, an antineoplastic agent with clinical uses in several malignancies, including tumors of the breast, ovary, prostate, and lung. Despite ongoing research, effective therapies for CINP remain limited. Thus, this preclinical study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of aerobic interval exercise (EX) with/without hesperidin (HES) on paclitaxel-induced neuropathic pain in rats. METHODS: Thirty male Wistar rats were randomly divided into five groups (n = 6): sham, paclitaxel (PTX), PTX with exercise (EX), PTX with HES (100 mg/kg), and PTX with EX and HES. PTX (2 mg/kg) was injected intraperitoneally on days 0, 2, 4, 6, and 8 of the study protocol. HES (100 mg/kg) was administered orally 5 days/week (days 14-35). The exercise training protocol (7 min running at 13-16 m/min, 5 days/week) was initiated after a 1-week acclimation period (day - 7) and continued throughout the study. Mechanical allodynia and thermal hyperalgesia tests were conducted at 8 time points: baseline (day - 14) and on days - 7, 0, 7, 14, 21, 28, and 35 to evaluate the rats' response to treatment. The animals were finally sacrificed, and their spinal cord tissues were used to determine the expression levels of several inflammatory and oxidative stress cytokines, interleukin (IL)-6, IL-10, tumor necrosis factor-α, malondialdehyde, and glutathione. RESULTS: Treatment with EX or HES alone significantly decreased mechanical allodynia (paw withdrawal threshold increased; p < 0.01) and thermal hyperalgesia (withdrawal latency increased; p < 0.001). Combined EX + HES treatment showed enhanced effects, with further improvements in both mechanical allodynia (p < 0.001 vs. either treatment alone) and thermal hyperalgesia (p < 0.001 vs. either treatment alone). The PTX-induced weight loss was significantly attenuated by EX (p < 0.01) and HES (p < 0.05), with the combination showing additive effects (p < 0.001 vs. PTX). Regarding biochemical markers, EX + HES combination demonstrated significant reduction in inflammatory cytokines and oxidative stress markers, while synergistically increasing anti-inflammatory and antioxidant markers. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings support the hypothesis that treadmill exercise with/without HES suppresses neuropathic pain and inflammatory and oxidative stress factors strongly affected by chemotherapies. Thus, this therapeutic protocol might be an alternative candidate for the management of paclitaxel-induced neuropathy. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

articles.title: Modulation of lincRNA-p21/mitomiR-181 and mitomiR-23b/SIRT1 signaling pathways in rotenone-induced neurodegeneration rat model.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuronal loss and α-synuclein-rich Lewy body accumulation. Mitochondrial dysfunction and microRNA (miRNA) dysregulation, particularly mitochondrial miRNAs (mitomiRs), are critical drivers of PD pathogenesis. METHODS: This study investigated the neuroprotective efficacy of the SGLT2 inhibitor, dapagliflozin, against rotenone-induced neurotoxicity, focusing on the lincRNA-p21/mitomiR-181/PTEN and mitomiR-23b/SIRT1/AMPK signaling axes. Male Wistar rats were randomized into three groups: a control group, a PD model group received rotenone (2 mg/kg every 48 h, s.c.), and a treatment group received rotenone plus dapagliflozin (10 mg/kg/day, p.o.) for 28 days. RESULTS: In the inducted rotenone group lincRNA-p21 sponges mir-181 which leads to the upregulation of PTEN which inhibits the conversion of PIP2 to PIP3 thus downregulating AKT expression and subsequent activation of GSK-3β kinase enzyme which increases α-synuclein accumulation. In addition, the PD-control group showed upregulation of Mitomir-23b with subsequent downregulation of SIRT-1 expression and inactivation of LKB1. Accompanied by inhibition of AMPK phosphorylation which in turn prevents the degradation of accumulated α-synuclein. Dapagliflozin treatment upregulates mir-181 and downregulates mitomir-23b, which restores DJ-1 levels, which in turn activate the antioxidant genes HO-1 and PINK1, and improve mitochondrial function. CONCLUSIONS: Dapagliflozin exerts neuroprotection by restoring lincRNA-p21/mitomiR-181/PTEN and mitomiR-23b/SIRT1/AMPK homeostasis, thereby inhibiting α-synuclein proteotoxicity and mitigating oxidative stress and neuroinflammation.

articles.title: BGN4-derived intestinal metabolite 6-hydroxynicotinic acid alleviates hepatocytes ferroptosis in MAFLD via Nrf2/SREBP1/CYP2E1 axis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is closely associated with dysbiosis of the gut microbiota. In this study, we investigated the biological effects and underlying mechanisms of Bifidobacterium bifidum BGN4 and its intestinal metabolite, 6-hydroxynicotinic acid (6-HNA), in regulating hepatocyte ferroptosis in MAFLD. METHODS: A MAFLD mouse model was established by administration of a high-fat diet. Serum biochemical parameters were measured, and liver histopathological injury was assessed by hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and Masson staining. Hepatocyte apoptosis was evaluated using TUNEL staining. Oxidative stress markers were quantified using ELISA, flow cytometry, and DCFH-DA staining, respectively. Cell viability and apoptosis were assessed by Cell Counting Kit-8 assay and flow cytometry. Intracellular Fe²⁺ and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels were measured using commercial assay kits. The acetylation level of the SREBP1 promoter was determined by chromatin immunoprecipitation. RESULTS: BGN4 significantly alleviated liver injury, oxidative stress, and hepatocyte ferroptosis in MAFLD mice. BGN4 treatment markedly increased the level of the intestinal metabolite 6-HNA. In vitro experiments further demonstrated that 6-HNA exerted a protective effect against palmitic acid (PA)-induced hepatocyte ferroptosis and oxidative stress. Mechanistically, 6-HNA activated Nrf2 signaling, thereby suppressing the SREBP1/CYP2E1 axis through reduction of p300-mediated histone acetylation. Rescue experiments showed that treatment with ML-385 or overexpression of SREBP1 reversed the protective effects of 6-HNA on PA-induced hepatocyte ferroptosis and oxidative stress. CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings indicate that the protective effects of BGN4 against hepatocyte ferroptosis and oxidative stress in MAFLD are likely associated with the upregulation of intestinal metabolite 6-HNA, which appears to modulate the Nrf2/SREBP1/CYP2E1 signaling axis, thereby supporting the therapeutic potential of the "probiotic-metabolite-liver" regulatory axis in MAFLD.
